māṃ viddhyanaṃtaṃ pārtha tvaṃ viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ haraṃ śivam.. 8 ..
4.94.d:
दानवानां विनाशाय वसुदेवकुलोद्भवम् ॥
मां विद्ध्यनंतं पार्थ त्वं विष्णुं जिष्णुं हरं शिवम्॥ 8 ॥
4.94.m: born in the lineage of Vasudeva for the destruction of the Dānavas. / Know me, O son of Pṛthā, to be Ananta, Viṣṇu, the victorious Jiṣṇu, Hara, Śiva,

4.94.s:
brahmāṇaṃ bhāskaraṃ śeṣaṃ sarvavyāpinamīśvaram ..
viśvarūpaṃ mahātmānaṃ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakārakam .. 9 ..
4.94.d:
ब्रह्माणं भास्करं शेषं सर्वव्यापिनमीश्वरम् ॥
विश्वरूपं महात्मानं सृष्टिसंहारकारकम् ॥ 9 ॥
4.94.m: Brahmā, the Sun, Śeṣa, the all-pervading Lord, / of universal form, the Great Self, the author of creation and dissolution.

4.94.s:
pratyayārthaṃ mayākhyātaṃ so'haṃ pārtha na saṃśayaḥ ..
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
anantavratamāhātmyavidhiṃ vada vidāṃ vara .. 10 ..
4.94.d:
प्रत्ययार्थं मयाख्यातं सोऽहं पार्थ न संशयः ॥
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
अनन्तव्रतमाहात्म्यविधिं वद विदां वर ॥ 10 ॥
4.94.m: I have told you this for the sake of conviction; I am he, O son of Pṛthā, without doubt." / Yudhiṣṭhira said: / "Tell me the rules and the greatness of the Ananta votive observance, O best of the knowers.

4.94.s:
kiṃ puṇyaṃ kiṃ phalaṃ cāsya hyanuṣṭhānavatāṃ nṛṇām..
kena vādau purā cīrṇaṃ martye kena prakāśitam .. 11 ..
4.94.d:
किं पुण्यं किं फलं चास्य ह्यनुष्ठानवतां नृणाम्॥
केन वादौ पुरा चीर्णं मर्त्ये केन प्रकाशितम् ॥ 11 ॥
4.94.m: What is the merit and what is the fruit of this for men who perform it? / By whom was it previously observed in ancient times, and by whom was it revealed among mortals?

4.94.s:
evaṃ samastaṃ vistārya brūhyanaṃtavrataṃ hare ..
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
āsītpurā kṛtayuge sumaṃto nāma vai dvijaḥ ..12..
4.94.d:
एवं समस्तं विस्तार्य ब्रूह्यनंतव्रतं हरे ॥
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
आसीत्पुरा कृतयुगे सुमंतो नाम वै द्विजः ॥12॥
4.94.m: Relating all of this in detail, tell me of the Ananta votive observance, O Hari." / The blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / "Long ago in the Kṛta age there was a twice-born named Sumanta,

4.94.s:
vaśiṣṭhagotre cotpannaḥ surūpaśca bhṛgoḥ sutām ..
dīkṣāṃ nāmopayeme tāṃ vedoktavidhinā tataḥ ..13..
4.94.d:
वशिष्ठगोत्रे चोत्पन्नः सुरूपश्च भृगोः सुताम् ॥
दीक्षां नामोपयेमे तां वेदोक्तविधिना ततः ॥13॥
4.94.m: handsome, born in the lineage of Vasiṣṭha. In accordance with the injunctions stated in the Vedas, / he then married a daughter of Bhṛgu named Dīkṣā.

4.94.s:
tasyāḥ kālena saṃjātā duhitānaṃtalakṣaṇā ..
śīlā nāma suśīlā sā vardhate pitṛsadmani .. 14 ..
4.94.d:
तस्याः कालेन संजाता दुहितानंतलक्षणा ॥
शीला नाम सुशीला सा वर्धते पितृसद्मनि ॥ 14 ॥
4.94.m: In time, a daughter endowed with endless good marks was born to her, / named Śīlā. Virtuous in character, she grew up in her father's house.

4.94.s:
mātā ca tasyāḥ kālena haradāhena pīḍitā ..
vinanāśa nadītīre mṛtā svargapuraṃ yayau..15..
4.94.d:
माता च तस्याः कालेन हरदाहेन पीडिता ॥
विननाश नदीतीरे मृता स्वर्गपुरं ययौ॥15॥
4.94.m: In the course of time, afflicted by a burning fever, her mother / passed away on the bank of a river, and dying, went to the city of heaven.

4.94.s:
sumaṃtopi tatonyāṃ vai dharmapuṃsaḥ sutāṃ punaḥ ..
upayeme vidhānena karkaśāṃ nāma nāmataḥ..16..
4.94.d:
सुमंतोपि ततोन्यां वै धर्मपुंसः सुतां पुनः ॥
उपयेमे विधानेन कर्कशां नाम नामतः॥16॥
4.94.m: Then Sumanta again married according to rule another woman, / a daughter of Dharmapums named Karkaśā.

4.94.s:
duḥśīlāṃ karkaśāṃ caṃḍīṃ nityaṃ kalahakāriṇīm ..
sāpi śīlā piturgehe gṛhārcanaratā vibho .. 17 ..
4.94.d:
दुःशीलां कर्कशां चंडीं नित्यं कलहकारिणीम् ॥
सापि शीला पितुर्गेहे गृहार्चनरता विभो ॥ 17 ॥
4.94.m: She was ill-behaved, harsh, fierce, and constantly quarrelsome. / Śīlā, too, O Lord, stayed in her father's house, devoted to household worship.

4.94.s:
kuḍyastaṃbhatulādhāradehalītoraṇādiṣu ..
cāturvarṇakaraṃ vaiśyanīlapītasitāsitaiḥ ..18..
4.94.d:
कुड्यस्तंभतुलाधारदेहलीतोरणादिषु ॥
चातुर्वर्णकरं वैश्यनीलपीतसितासितैः ॥18॥
4.94.m: On the walls, pillars, crossbeams, thresholds, archways, and other places, / she made [designs] of the four colours with dark blue, yellow, white, and black,

4.94.s:
svastikaiḥ śaṃkhapadmaiśca arcayantī punaḥpunaḥ ..
pitrā dṛṣṭā sumantena strīcihnā yauvane sthitā ..19..
4.94.d:
स्वस्तिकैः शंखपद्मैश्च अर्चयन्ती पुनःपुनः ॥
पित्रा दृष्टा सुमन्तेन स्त्रीचिह्ना यौवने स्थिता ॥19॥
4.94.m: worshipping again and again with svastikas, conches, and lotuses. / She was seen by her father Sumanta possessing womanly signs, arrived at youth.

4.94.s:
kasmai deyā mayā śīlā vicāryaivaṃ suduḥkhitaḥ ..
pitā dadau munīndrāya kauṃḍinyāya śubhe dine .. 20 ..
4.94.d:
कस्मै देया मया शीला विचार्यैवं सुदुःखितः ॥
पिता ददौ मुनीन्द्राय कौंडिन्याय शुभे दिने ॥ 20 ॥
4.94.m: "To whom should Śīlā be given by me?" Thinking thus, he became deeply distressed. / On an auspicious day, the father gave her to the lord of sages, Kauṇḍinya.

4.94.s:
smṛtyuktaśāstravidhinā vivāhamakarottadā ..
nivartyodvāhikaṃ sarvaṃ proktavānkarkaśāṃ dvijaḥ .. 21 ..
4.94.d:
स्मृत्युक्तशास्त्रविधिना विवाहमकरोत्तदा ॥
निवर्त्योद्वाहिकं सर्वं प्रोक्तवान्कर्कशां द्विजः ॥ 21 ॥
4.94.m: He then performed the wedding according to the rules of the treatises of sacred tradition. / Having concluded all the marriage rites, the twice-born said to Karkaśā:

4.94.s:
kiñcidāyādikaṃ deyaṃ jāmātuḥ pāritoṣikam ..
tacchrutvā karkaśā kruddhā proddhṛtya gṛhamaṇḍapam..22..
4.94.d:
किञ्चिदायादिकं देयं जामातुः पारितोषिकम् ॥
तच्छ्रुत्वा कर्कशा क्रुद्धा प्रोद्धृत्य गृहमण्डपम्॥22॥
4.94.m: "Some inheritance or the like should be given as a gift of gratification to the son-in-law." / Hearing that, Karkaśā became enraged, tore down the pavilion of the house,

4.94.s:
kapāṭe susthiraṃ kṛtvā gamyatāmityuvāca ha ..
bhojyāvaśiṣṭacūrṇena pātheyaṃ ca cakāra sā ..23..
4.94.d:
कपाटे सुस्थिरं कृत्वा गम्यतामित्युवाच ह ॥
भोज्यावशिष्टचूर्णेन पाथेयं च चकार सा ॥23॥
4.94.m: firmly fastened the two door-leaves, and said: "Begone!" / And from flour left over from food, she prepared provisions for the road.

4.94.s:
kauṃḍinyopi vivāhyaināṃ pathi gacchañchanaiḥśanaiḥ..
śīlāṃ suśīlāmādāya navoḍhāṃ gorathena hi .. 24 ..
4.94.d:
कौंडिन्योपि विवाह्यैनां पथि गच्छञ्छनैःशनैः॥
शीलां सुशीलामादाय नवोढां गोरथेन हि ॥ 24 ॥
4.94.m: Having married her, Kauṇḍinya, taking the newly-wed Śīlā, / who was exceedingly virtuous, went slowly along the road in an ox-cart.

4.94.s:
madhyāhne bhojyavelāyāṃ samuttīrya sarittaṭe ..
dadarśa śīlā sā strīṇāṃ samūhaṃ raktavāsasām.. .. 25 ..
4.94.d:
मध्याह्ने भोज्यवेलायां समुत्तीर्य सरित्तटे ॥
ददर्श शीला सा स्त्रीणां समूहं रक्तवाससाम्॥ ॥ 25 ॥
4.94.m: At midday, at the time for meals, having stepped down onto a riverbank, / Śīlā saw a group of women dressed in red garments

4.94.s:
caturdaśyāmarcayantaṃ bhaktyā devaṃ pṛthakpṛthak ..
upagamya śanaiḥ śīlā papraccha strīkadaṃbakam.. 26 ..
4.94.d:
चतुर्दश्यामर्चयन्तं भक्त्या देवं पृथक्पृथक् ॥
उपगम्य शनैः शीला पप्रच्छ स्त्रीकदंबकम्॥ 26 ॥
4.94.m: worshipping the god individually with devotion on the fourteenth [lunar day]. / Approaching slowly, Śīlā asked the gathering of women:

4.94.s:
nāryaḥ kimetanme brūta kiṃnāma vratamīdṛśam ..
tā ūcuryoṣitaḥ sarvā ananto nāma viśrutaḥ .. 27 ..
4.94.d:
नार्यः किमेतन्मे ब्रूत किंनाम व्रतमीदृशम् ॥
ता ऊचुर्योषितः सर्वा अनन्तो नाम विश्रुतः ॥ 27 ॥
4.94.m: "O women, tell me what this is: what is the name of such a votive observance?" / All those women said to her: "He is renowned by the name Ananta."

4.94.s:
sābravīdahamapyevaṃ kariṣye vratamuttamam ..
vidhānaṃ kīdṛśaṃ tatra kiṃ dānaṃ kasya pūjanam .. 28 ..
4.94.d:
साब्रवीदहमप्येवं करिष्ये व्रतमुत्तमम् ॥
विधानं कीदृशं तत्र किं दानं कस्य पूजनम् ॥ 28 ॥
4.94.m: She said: "I too will perform this supreme votive observance in this manner. / What is the rule for it? What is the gift? Whose worship [is performed]?"

4.94.s:
.. striya ūcuḥ .. ..
śīle pakvānnaprasthasya punnāmnaḥ sukṛtasya tu ..
arddhaṃ viprāya dātavyamarddhamātmani bhojanam .. 29 ..
4.94.d:
॥ स्त्रिय ऊचुः ॥ ॥
शीले पक्वान्नप्रस्थस्य पुन्नाम्नः सुकृतस्य तु ॥
अर्द्धं विप्राय दातव्यमर्द्धमात्मनि भोजनम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.94.m: The women said: / "O Śīlā, of a prastha of cooked food, well made and bearing a male name, / half should be given to a Brahmin, and half is for eating oneself.

4.94.s:
kartavyaṃ tu sarittīre kathāṃ śrutvā harerimām ..
anaṃtānaṃtamabhyarcya maṃḍale gaṃdhadīpakaiḥ .. 30 ..
4.94.d:
कर्तव्यं तु सरित्तीरे कथां श्रुत्वा हरेरिमाम् ॥
अनंतानंतमभ्यर्च्य मंडले गंधदीपकैः ॥ 30 ॥
4.94.m: It should be performed on a riverbank after hearing this story of Hari, / having worshipped Ananta, the boundless, on a maṇḍala with perfumes, lamps,

4.94.s:
dhūpaiḥ puṣpaiḥ sanaivedyaiḥ pītālaktaiścatuḥśataiḥ ..
tasyāgrato dṛḍhaṃ sūtraṃ kuṃkumāktaṃ sudorakam .. 31 ..
4.94.d:
धूपैः पुष्पैः सनैवेद्यैः पीतालक्तैश्चतुःशतैः ॥
तस्याग्रतो दृढं सूत्रं कुंकुमाक्तं सुदोरकम् ॥ 31 ॥
4.94.m: incense, flowers, food offerings, and four hundred yellow lac marks. / In front of him, a strong cord smeared with saffron, an excellent thread

4.94.s:
caturdaśagraṃthiyutaṃ vāme strī dakṣiṇe pumān ..
maṃtreṇānena rājendra yāvadvarṣaṃ samāpyate .. 32 ..
4.94.d:
चतुर्दशग्रंथियुतं वामे स्त्री दक्षिणे पुमान् ॥
मंत्रेणानेन राजेन्द्र यावद्वर्षं समाप्यते ॥ 32 ॥
4.94.m: furnished with fourteen knots, [should be tied] on the left [arm] for a woman, and on the right for a man, / with this mantra, O lord of kings, until the year is completed:

4.94.s:
anaṃta saṃsāramahāsamudre magnānsamabhyuddhara vāsudeva ..
anaṃtarūpe viniyojitātmā hyanaṃtarūpāya namonamaste .. 33 ..
4.94.d:
अनंत संसारमहासमुद्रे मग्नान्समभ्युद्धर वासुदेव ॥
अनंतरूपे विनियोजितात्मा ह्यनंतरूपाय नमोनमस्ते ॥ 33 ॥
4.94.m: 'O Ananta, rescue those submerged in the great ocean of cyclic existence, O Vāsudeva! / Having applied my soul to your infinite form, homage, homage to you whose form is infinite!'

4.94.s:
anena dorakaṃ baddhvā bhoktavyaṃ svasthamānasaiḥ ..
dhyātvā nārāyaṇaṃ devamanaṃtaṃ viśvarūpiṇam .. 34 ..
4.94.d:
अनेन दोरकं बद्ध्वा भोक्तव्यं स्वस्थमानसैः ॥
ध्यात्वा नारायणं देवमनंतं विश्वरूपिणम् ॥ 34 ॥
4.94.m: Having bound the cord with this [mantra], food should be eaten with tranquil minds, / having meditated upon the god Nārāyaṇa, Ananta, whose form is the universe.

4.94.s:
bhuktvā cāṃte vrajedveśma hīdaṃ proktaṃ vrataṃ tava ..
sāpi śrutvā vrataṃ cakre śīlā baddhvā sudorakam .. 35 ..
4.94.d:
भुक्त्वा चांते व्रजेद्वेश्म हीदं प्रोक्तं व्रतं तव ॥
सापि श्रुत्वा व्रतं चक्रे शीला बद्ध्वा सुदोरकम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.94.m: And having eaten, one should go home at the conclusion; this votive observance has been described to you." / Having heard it, Śīlā also performed the observance and tied the excellent cord.

4.94.s:
bhartā tasyāḥ samāgatya tāṃ dadarśa mahādhanām ..
pātheyaśeṣaṃ viprāya dattvā bhuktvā tathaiva ca .. 36 ..
4.94.d:
भर्ता तस्याः समागत्य तां ददर्श महाधनाम् ॥
पाथेयशेषं विप्राय दत्त्वा भुक्त्वा तथैव च ॥ 36 ॥
4.94.m: Her husband, having arrived, saw her possessed of great wealth. / Giving the remainder of the travel provisions to a Brahmin and eating likewise,

4.94.s:
punarjagāma sā hṛṣṭā gorathena svamāśramam ..
bhartrā sahaiva śanakaiḥ pratyakṣaṃ tatkṣaṇādabhūt ..
tenānaṃtaprabhāveṇa śubhagodhanasaṃkulaḥ .. 37 ..
4.94.d:
पुनर्जगाम सा हृष्टा गोरथेन स्वमाश्रमम् ॥
भर्त्रा सहैव शनकैः प्रत्यक्षं तत्क्षणादभूत् ॥
तेनानंतप्रभावेण शुभगोधनसंकुलः ॥ 37 ॥
4.94.m: she went again, joyful, in the ox-cart to her own hermitage / slowly along with her husband. Instantly it became evident: / through the power of Ananta, [the hermitage] was filled with auspicious cattle wealth.

4.94.s:
gṛhāśramaḥ śriyā yukto dhanadhānyasamāyutaḥ ..
ākulo vyākulo ramyaḥ sarvatrātithipūjanaḥ .. 38 ..
4.94.d:
गृहाश्रमः श्रिया युक्तो धनधान्यसमायुतः ॥
आकुलो व्याकुलो रम्यः सर्वत्रातिथिपूजनः ॥ 38 ॥
4.94.m: The household hermitage was endowed with fortune, supplied with wealth and grain, / bustling, lively, pleasant, and everywhere honouring guests.

4.94.s:
sāpi māṇikyakāñcībhirmuktāhāravibhūṣitā ..
divyāṃgavastrasaṃchannā sāvitrīpratimābhavat .. 39 ..
4.94.d:
सापि माणिक्यकाञ्चीभिर्मुक्ताहारविभूषिता ॥
दिव्यांगवस्त्रसंछन्ना सावित्रीप्रतिमाभवत् ॥ 39 ॥
4.94.m: She too, adorned with ruby girdles and pearl necklaces, / covered in garments for celestial bodies, became like Sāvitrī.

4.94.s:
kadācidupaviṣṭena dṛṣṭaṃ baddhaṃ sudorakam ..
śīlāyā hastamūle tu sākṣepaṃ troṭitaṃ ruṣā .. 40 ..
4.94.d:
कदाचिदुपविष्टेन दृष्टं बद्धं सुदोरकम् ॥
शीलाया हस्तमूले तु साक्षेपं त्रोटितं रुषा ॥ 40 ॥
4.94.m: Once, as he sat, the excellent cord tied / at the root of Śīlā's hand was seen [by him], and with reproach he broke it in anger.

4.94.s:
tena karmavipākeṇa tasya sā śrīḥ kṣayaṃ gatā ..
godhanaṃ taskarairnītaṃ gṛhaṃ cāgnividāhitam .. 41 ..
4.94.d:
तेन कर्मविपाकेण तस्य सा श्रीः क्षयं गता ॥
गोधनं तस्करैर्नीतं गृहं चाग्निविदाहितम् ॥ 41 ॥
4.94.m: By the fruition of that deed, that prosperity of his went to ruin: / the cattle wealth was taken by thieves, and the house was burned by fire.

4.94.s:
yadyadevāgataṃ gehe tatra tatraiva naśyati ..
svajanaiḥ kalaho mitrairvacanaṃ na janaistathā .. 42 ..
4.94.d:
यद्यदेवागतं गेहे तत्र तत्रैव नश्यति ॥
स्वजनैः कलहो मित्रैर्वचनं न जनैस्तथा ॥ 42 ॥
4.94.m: Whatever entered his house perished right there and then. / There were quarrels with relatives and friends, and people would not speak [to him].

4.94.s:
anaṃtākṣepadoṣeṇa dāridryaṃ patitaṃ gṛhe ..
na kaścidvadate lokastena sārddhaṃ yudhiṣṭhira .. 43 ..
4.94.d:
अनंताक्षेपदोषेण दारिद्र्यं पतितं गृहे ॥
न कश्चिद्वदते लोकस्तेन सार्द्धं युधिष्ठिर ॥ 43 ॥
4.94.m: Through the fault of scorning Ananta, poverty fell upon his house. / No one spoke with him, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

4.94.s:
tato jagāma kauṃḍinyo nirvedādvanagahvaram ..
manasā dhyāyatenaṃtaṃ kadā drakṣyāmi keśavam .. 44 ..
4.94.d:
ततो जगाम कौंडिन्यो निर्वेदाद्वनगह्वरम् ॥
मनसा ध्यायतेनंतं कदा द्रक्ष्यामि केशवम् ॥ 44 ॥
4.94.m: Then, out of despondency, Kauṇḍinya went into the depths of the forest, / meditating in his mind upon Ananta: “When shall I see Keśava?”

4.94.s:
vrataṃ niraśanaṃ gṛhya brahmacaryaṃ japanharim ..
vihvalaḥ prayayau pārtha araṇyaṃ janavarjitam..45..
4.94.d:
व्रतं निरशनं गृह्य ब्रह्मचर्यं जपन्हरिम् ॥
विह्वलः प्रययौ पार्थ अरण्यं जनवर्जितम्॥45॥
4.94.m: Undertaking a fast as his votive observance, practicing celibacy, murmuring Hari's names, / he wandered, distraught, into the wilderness devoid of men, O Pārtha.

4.94.s:
tatrāpaśyanmahāvṛkṣaṃ phalitaṃ puṣpitaṃ tathā ..
tamapṛcchattvayānaṃtaḥ kaccidṛṣṭo mahādruma ..
tadbrūhi sopyuvācedaṃ nānaṃtaṃ vedmyahaṃ dvija .. 46 ..
4.94.d:
तत्रापश्यन्महावृक्षं फलितं पुष्पितं तथा ॥
तमपृच्छत्त्वयानंतः कच्चिदृष्टो महाद्रुम ॥
तद्ब्रूहि सोप्युवाचेदं नानंतं वेद्म्यहं द्विज ॥ 46 ॥
4.94.m: There he saw a great tree, laden with fruit and in full bloom. / He asked it: “O great tree, have you seen Ananta? / Tell me that!” But it replied: “I do not know Ananta, O twice-born one.”

4.94.s:
evaṃ nirīkṣitastena gāṃ dadarśa savatsakām ..
tṛṇamadhye pradhāvantīmitaścetaśca pāṃḍava ..47..
4.94.d:
एवं निरीक्षितस्तेन गां ददर्श सवत्सकाम् ॥
तृणमध्ये प्रधावन्तीमितश्चेतश्च पांडव ॥47॥
4.94.m: Having looked upon it thus, he saw a cow with her calf / running here and there in the middle of the grass, O descendant of Pāṇḍu.

4.94.s:
sobravīddhenuke brūhi yadyanaṃtastvayekṣitaḥ ..
gauruvācātha kauṃḍinya nānaṃtaṃ vedmyahaṃ vibho .. 48 ..
4.94.d:
सोब्रवीद्धेनुके ब्रूहि यद्यनंतस्त्वयेक्षितः ॥
गौरुवाचाथ कौंडिन्य नानंतं वेद्म्यहं विभो ॥ 48 ॥
4.94.m: He said: “O gentle cow, tell me if Ananta has been seen by you.” / Then the cow said: “O Kauṇḍinya, I do not know Ananta, O lord.”

4.94.s:
tato jagāmātha vane govṛṣaṃ śādvale sthitam ..
dṛṣṭvā papraccha gosvāminnanaṃto lakṣitastvayā .. 49 ..
4.94.d:
ततो जगामाथ वने गोवृषं शाद्वले स्थितम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छ गोस्वामिन्ननंतो लक्षितस्त्वया ॥ 49 ॥
4.94.m: Then he went into the forest and, seeing an ox standing on a meadow, / he asked: “O lord of cattle, have you noticed Ananta?”

4.94.s:
govṛṣastamuvācātha nānanto vīkṣito mayā ..
tato vrajandadarśāgre ramyaṃ puṣkariṇīdvayam .. 50 ..
4.94.d:
गोवृषस्तमुवाचाथ नानन्तो वीक्षितो मया ॥
ततो व्रजन्ददर्शाग्रे रम्यं पुष्करिणीद्वयम् ॥ 50 ॥
4.94.m: The ox then said to him: “I have not seen Ananta.” / Then, walking on, he saw ahead two lovely lotus pools,

4.94.s:
anyonyajalakallolavīcibhiḥ pariśobhitam ..
channaṃ kumudakahlāraiḥ kumudotpalamaṃḍitam .. 51 ..
4.94.d:
अन्योन्यजलकल्लोलवीचिभिः परिशोभितम् ॥
छन्नं कुमुदकह्लारैः कुमुदोत्पलमंडितम् ॥ 51 ॥
4.94.m: adorned with waves from the billows of each other's waters, / covered with white water lilies and red water lilies, decorated with day-blooming lotuses and blue lotuses,

4.94.s:
sevitaṃ bhramarairhaṃsaiścakraiḥ kāraṃḍavairbakaiḥ ..
te apṛcchaṃ dvijonanto bhavadbhyāṃ nopalakṣitaḥ .. 52 ..
4.94.d:
सेवितं भ्रमरैर्हंसैश्चक्रैः कारंडवैर्बकैः ॥
ते अपृच्छं द्विजोनन्तो भवद्भ्यां नोपलक्षितः ॥ 52 ॥
4.94.m: frequented by bees, geese, cakravākas, kāraṇḍava ducks, and herons. / The twice-born asked them: “Has Ananta not been perceived by you two?”

4.94.s:
ūcatuḥ puṣkariṇyau taṃ nānaṃtaṃ vidvahe dvija ..
tato brahmandadarśāgre gardabhaṃ kuñjaraṃ tathā .. 53 ..
4.94.d:
ऊचतुः पुष्करिण्यौ तं नानंतं विद्वहे द्विज ॥
ततो ब्रह्मन्ददर्शाग्रे गर्दभं कुञ्जरं तथा ॥ 53 ॥
4.94.m: The two lotus pools said to him: “We do not know Ananta, O twice-born one.” / Then, O Brahmin, he saw ahead a donkey and also an elephant.

4.94.s:
tāvapyuktau sumaṃtena tasyāpi viniveditam ..
nāvābhyāṃ vīkṣitonaṃtastacchrutvā niṣasāda ha .. 54 ..
4.94.d:
तावप्युक्तौ सुमंतेन तस्यापि विनिवेदितम् ॥
नावाभ्यां वीक्षितोनंतस्तच्छ्रुत्वा निषसाद ह ॥ 54 ॥
4.94.m: Those two were also addressed by Sumanta, and they also declared: / “Ananta has not been seen by the two of us.” Hearing that, he sank down.

4.94.s:
tasminkṣaṇe munivare kauṃḍinye brāhmaṇottame ..
kṛpayānaṃtadevopi pratyakṣaḥ samajāyata .. .. 55 ..
4.94.d:
तस्मिन्क्षणे मुनिवरे कौंडिन्ये ब्राह्मणोत्तमे ॥
कृपयानंतदेवोपि प्रत्यक्षः समजायत ॥ ॥ 55 ॥
4.94.m: At that moment, toward that best of sages Kauṇḍinya, the excellent Brahmin, / Lord Ananta out of compassion appeared visibly.

4.94.s:
vṛddhabrāhmaṇarūpeṇa ita ehītyuvāca tam ..
praveśayitvā svagṛhaṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe kare .. 56 ..
4.94.d:
वृद्धब्राह्मणरूपेण इत एहीत्युवाच तम् ॥
प्रवेशयित्वा स्वगृहं गृहीत्वा दक्षिणे करे ॥ 56 ॥
4.94.m: In the form of an old Brahmin, he said to him: “Come here!” / Taking him by the right hand, and leading him into his house,

4.94.s:
tāṃ purīṃ darśayāmāsa divyanārīnarairyutām ..
tasyāṃ niviṣṭamātmānaṃ varasiṃhāsane nṛpa .. 57 ..
4.94.d:
तां पुरीं दर्शयामास दिव्यनारीनरैर्युताम् ॥
तस्यां निविष्टमात्मानं वरसिंहासने नृप ॥ 57 ॥
4.94.m: he showed him that city filled with divine women and men, / and his own self seated within it upon an excellent throne, O king,

4.94.s:
pārśvasthaśaṃkhacakrāsigadāgaruḍaśobhitam ..
darśayāmāsa viprāya pūrvoktaṃ viśvarūpiṇam.. 58 ..
4.94.d:
पार्श्वस्थशंखचक्रासिगदागरुडशोभितम् ॥
दर्शयामास विप्राय पूर्वोक्तं विश्वरूपिणम्॥ 58 ॥
4.94.m: adorned by the conch, discus, sword, mace, and Garuḍa standing beside him; / he revealed to the Brahmin his previously described universal form,

4.94.s:
vibhūtibhedaiścānantamanantaṃ parameśvaram ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu dvijonantamuvāca parayā mudā .. 59 ..
4.94.d:
विभूतिभेदैश्चानन्तमनन्तं परमेश्वरम् ॥
तं दृष्ट्वा तु द्विजोनन्तमुवाच परया मुदा ॥ 59 ॥
4.94.m: infinite through diverse manifestations of sovereign power, the endless Supreme Lord. / Seeing him, Ananta, the twice-born spoke with supreme joy:

4.94.s:
pāpohaṃ pāpakarmāhaṃ pāpātmā pāpasambhavaḥ ..
pāhi māṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa sarvapāpaharo bhava ..60..
4.94.d:
पापोहं पापकर्माहं पापात्मा पापसम्भवः ॥
पाहि मां पुण्डरीकाक्ष सर्वपापहरो भव ॥60॥
4.94.m: “I am a sinner, my actions are sinful, my soul is sinful, I was born of sin; / protect me, O lotus-eyed one! Be the destroyer of all my sins!

4.94.s:
adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ ca sujīvitam ..
cūtavṛkṣo vṛṣaḥ kastu kā gauḥ puṣkariṇīdvayam ..
gardabhaṃ kuñjaraṃ caiva deva me brūhi tattvataḥ .. 61 ..
4.94.d:
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म जीवितं च सुजीवितम् ॥
चूतवृक्षो वृषः कस्तु का गौः पुष्करिणीद्वयम् ॥
गर्दभं कुञ्जरं चैव देव मे ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः ॥ 61 ॥
4.94.m: Today my birth is fruitful, and my life is well-lived! / But who was the mango tree, who was the ox, who the cow, what were the two lotus pools, / what was the donkey, and what the elephant? O Lord, tell me this in truth!”

4.94.s:
.. anaṃta uvāca .. ..
cūtavṛkṣo hi viprosau vidvānyo vedagarvitaḥ ..
vidyādānaṃ nopakurvañchiṣyebhyastarutāṃ gataḥ .. 62 ..
4.94.d:
॥ अनंत उवाच ॥ ॥
चूतवृक्षो हि विप्रोसौ विद्वान्यो वेदगर्वितः ॥
विद्यादानं नोपकुर्वञ्छिष्येभ्यस्तरुतां गतः ॥ 62 ॥
4.94.m: Ananta said: / “The mango tree was a Brahmin, a learned man puffed up with pride in the Vedas; / not imparting his learning to disciples, he was turned into a tree.

4.94.s:
sā gaurvasundharā dṛṣṭā niṣphalā yā tvayekṣitā ..
sa harṣo vṛṣabho dṛṣṭo lābhārthaṃ yastvayā vṛtaḥ .. 63 ..
4.94.d:
सा गौर्वसुन्धरा दृष्टा निष्फला या त्वयेक्षिता ॥
स हर्षो वृषभो दृष्टो लाभार्थं यस्त्वया वृतः ॥ 63 ॥
4.94.m: The cow seen by you, which was barren, was the earth. / The ox you saw and approached for gain was Joy.

4.94.s:
dharmādharmavyavasthānaṃ tacca puṣkariṇīdvayam ..
kharaḥ krodhastvayā dṛṣṭaḥ kuṃjaro dharmadūṣakaḥ ..
brāhmaṇosāvanaṃtohaṃ guhāsaṃsāragahvare .. 64 ..
4.94.d:
धर्माधर्मव्यवस्थानं तच्च पुष्करिणीद्वयम् ॥
खरः क्रोधस्त्वया दृष्टः कुंजरो धर्मदूषकः ॥
ब्राह्मणोसावनंतोहं गुहासंसारगह्वरे ॥ 64 ॥
4.94.m: The two lotus pools were the order of righteousness and unrighteousness. / The donkey seen by you was anger, and the elephant was the corruptor of righteousness. / That Brahmin was I, Ananta, dwelling in the secret cave in the depth of saṃsāra.

4.94.s: ityuktaṃ te mayā sarvaṃ vipra gaccha punargṛham .. 65 ..
4.94.d: इत्युक्तं ते मया सर्वं विप्र गच्छ पुनर्गृहम् ॥ 65 ॥
4.94.m: Thus all has been told to you by me. O Brahmin, go back home.

4.94.s:
carānaṃtavrataṃ tattvaṃ nava varṣāṇi paṃca ca ..
tatastuṣṭaḥ pradāsyāmi nakṣatrasthānamuttamam .. 66 ..
4.94.d:
चरानंतव्रतं तत्त्वं नव वर्षाणि पंच च ॥
ततस्तुष्टः प्रदास्यामि नक्षत्रस्थानमुत्तमम् ॥ 66 ॥
4.94.m: Perform the true votive observance of Ananta for fourteen years. / Then, pleased, I shall grant you the supreme station among the asterisms.

4.94.s:
bhuktvā ca vipulānbhogānsarvānkāmānyathepsitān ..
putrapautraiḥ parivṛtastato mokṣamavāpsyasi..67..
4.94.d:
भुक्त्वा च विपुलान्भोगान्सर्वान्कामान्यथेप्सितान् ॥
पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृतस्ततो मोक्षमवाप्स्यसि॥67॥
4.94.m: Having enjoyed abundant pleasures and all desires as wished, / surrounded by sons and grandsons, you will then attain liberation.”

4.94.s:
iti dattvā varaṃ devastatraivāṃtarhito'bhavat..
kauṃḍinyopyāgato gehaṃ cacārānaṃtasadvratam .. 68 ..
4.94.d:
इति दत्त्वा वरं देवस्तत्रैवांतर्हितोऽभवत्॥
कौंडिन्योप्यागतो गेहं चचारानंतसद्व्रतम् ॥ 68 ॥
4.94.m: Having thus granted the boon, the Lord vanished right there. / Kauṇḍinya also returned home and performed the virtuous votive observance of Ananta.

4.94.s:
śīlayā saha dharmātmā bhuktvā bhogānmanoramān..
aṃte jagāma ca svargaṃ nakṣatraṃ ca punarvasum ..
kalpasthānī ca saṃbhūto dṛśyatedyāpi sa jvalan. ..
anaṃtavratadharmeṇa samyakcīṇeṃna kaurava .. 70 ..
4.94.d:
शीलया सह धर्मात्मा भुक्त्वा भोगान्मनोरमान्॥
अंते जगाम च स्वर्गं नक्षत्रं च पुनर्वसुम् ॥
कल्पस्थानी च संभूतो दृश्यतेद्यापि स ज्वलन्॥।
अनंतव्रतधर्मेण सम्यक्चीणेंन कौरव ॥ 70 ॥
4.94.m: Together with Śīlā, the righteous-minded man enjoyed delightful pleasures, / and in the end went to heaven and to the asterism Punarvasu; / and having attained an enduring place for an eon, he is still seen shining today / through the virtue of the votive observance of Ananta properly performed, O descendant of Kuru.

4.94.s:
etatte kathitaṃ pārtha vratānāmuttamaṃ vratam ..
yatkṛtvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 71 ..
4.94.d:
एतत्ते कथितं पार्थ व्रतानामुत्तमं व्रतम् ॥
यत्कृत्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ 71 ॥
4.94.m: This, the highest of votive observances among all votive observances, has been told to you, O Pārtha, / by performing which one is freed from all sins, of this there is no doubt.

4.94.s:
ye ca śṛṇvaṃti satataṃ vācyamānaṃ narottama ..
te sarve pāpanirmuktā yāsyaṃti paramāṃ gatim .. 72 ..
4.94.d:
ये च शृण्वंति सततं वाच्यमानं नरोत्तम ॥
ते सर्वे पापनिर्मुक्ता यास्यंति परमां गतिम् ॥ 72 ॥
4.94.m: And those who constantly listen to it being recited, O best of men, / all of them, freed from sin, will go to the supreme state.

4.94.s:
saṃsārasāgaraguhāṃ susukhaṃ vihartuṃ vāṃchaṃti ye kurukulodbhava śuddhasattvāḥ ..

4.94.d:
संसारसागरगुहां सुसुखं विहर्तुं वांछंति ये कुरुकुलोद्भव शुद्धसत्त्वाः ॥
संपूज्य ते त्रिभुवनेशमनंतदेवं बध्नंति दक्षिणकरे वरदोरकं मे ॥ 73 ॥
4.94.m: Those of pure nature born in the Kuru lineage who desire to traverse with great ease the cave of the ocean of saṃsāra, / having worshipped the Lord of the three worlds, Lord Ananta, bind my excellent cord on their right hand.

4.94.s: iti śrībhaviṣye mahā'purāṇa uttaraparvaṇi śrīkṛṣṇayudhiṣṭhirasaṃvāde'anaṃtacaturdaśīvratavarṇanaṃ nāma caturnavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 94 .. cha ..
4.94.d: इति श्रीभविष्ये महाऽपुराण उत्तरपर्वणि श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवादेऽअनंतचतुर्दशीव्रतवर्णनं नाम चतुर्नवतितमोऽध्यायः ॥ 94 ॥ छ ॥
4.94.m: Thus ends the ninety-fourth chapter, named 'Description of the Anantacaturdaśī Votive Observance', in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira, in the Uttaraparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.

4.94.d:
शब्दकल्पद्रुम ---
अरण्यवासमुषितो युधिष्ठिरनृपो वशी ।
प्राप्तस्त्रैलोक्यनाथेन कृष्णेन परमात्मना ॥
कथोपकथनं जातं तयोस्तत्र प्रियाप्रियं ।
विशेषेण च गोविन्दं पप्रच्छ च युधिष्ठिरः ॥
युधिष्ठिर उवाच ।
केन व्रतेन देवेश वाञ्छितं प्राप्यते फलं ।
निष्पापाः सकला लोकाः भवन्ति जन्मजन्मनि ॥
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ।
अस्ति व्रतमनन्ताख्यं यत्कृतं सुरसद्मनि ।
इन्द्राद्यैर्लोकपालैश्च तन्म कथयतः शृणु ।
शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां मासि भाद्रपदे तथा ।
तस्यानुष्ठानमात्रेण सर्व्वपापं प्रणश्यति ॥
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ।
कृष्ण कोऽयं त्वयाख्यातो योऽनन्त इति संज्ञितः
कोऽयं शेषश्च नागश्च अनन्तस्तक्षकः स्मृतः ॥
परमञ्चोत्तमं वापि उताहो ब्रह्म उच्यते ।
क एषोऽनन्तसंज्ञो वै तन्मे ब्रूहि जनार्द्दन ॥
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ।
अनन्त इत्यहं पार्थ मम रूपं निबोध तत् ।
आदित्यगतिरूपेश यः काल उपपद्यते ॥
कलाकाष्ठामुहूर्त्तादि दिनरात्रिव्यवस्थया ।
पक्षो मास ऋतुर्व्वर्षं युगकल्पव्यवस्थया ॥
4.94.m: [Quotation from] Śabdakalpadruma: / King Yudhiṣṭhira, self-controlled, dwelling in forest exile, / was approached by Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Self and lord of the three worlds. / A conversation concerning agreeable and disagreeable matters took place between the two of them there, / and Yudhiṣṭhira especially questioned Govinda. / Yudhiṣṭhira said: / “By what votive observance, O Lord of gods, is the desired fruit attained, / and do all people become free from sin life after life?” / Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / “There is a votive observance named Ananta, which was performed in the abode of the gods / by Indra and the other world protectors; listen to it as I tell it. / On the fourteenth lunar day of the bright fortnight in the month of Bhādrapada, / merely by its performance all sin is destroyed.” / Yudhiṣṭhira said: / “O Kṛṣṇa, who is this one spoken of by you who is called Ananta? / Who is this Śeṣa, this serpent Ananta known as Takṣaka? / Or is the Supreme and highest Brahman spoken of? / Who indeed is this one called Ananta? Tell me that, O Janārdana.” / Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / “I am Ananta, O Pārtha; understand that to be my form: / that Time which manifests as the lord in the form of the sun’s course, / through the division of kalās, kāṣṭhās, muhūrtas, days, and nights, / fortnights, months, seasons, and years, arranged by yugas and kalpas.”

4.94.d:
सोऽहं कालोऽवतीर्णोऽस्मि भुवो भारावतारणात् ।
दानवानां विनाशाय वसुदेवतनूद्भवं ।!
अनन्तं विद्धि मां पार्थ कृष्णं विष्णुं हरिं शिवं
ब्रह्माणं भास्करं शेषं सर्व्वव्यापिनमीश्वरं ।
प्रत्ययार्थं मया पार्थ विश्वरूपं निबोथ तत् ।
पूर्वमेव महाबाहो योगिध्येयमनुत्तमं ॥ ॥
युधिष्ठिर उवाच ।
अनन्तव्रतमाहात्म्यं विधिं विधिविदां वर ।
किं पुण्यं किं फलं तस्य अनुष्ठानञ्च तस्य किं ॥
केन वा तत्कृतं पूर्व्वं लोके केन प्रकाशितं ।
तत्सर्व्वं बहु' विस्तार्य्य ब्रूहि नारायण प्रभो ॥
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ।
आसीत्पुरा कृतयुगे सुमन्तुर्नाम वै द्विजः ।
वशिष्ठगोत्रजो विद्वान् शीलवान् विजितेन्द्रियः ॥
पत्नी तस्याभवद्दीक्षा सती सत्यव्रते स्थिता ।
चारित्रशीलसम्पन्ना सुरूपा भृगुवंशजा ॥
तस्याः कालेन संजाता दुहिता सर्व्वलक्षणा ।
शीला नाम्ना सुशीला सा वर्द्धते पितृवेश्मनि ॥
4.94.m:
I am Time, descended to lighten the burden of the earth, / born of Vasudeva to destroy the Danavas. / Know Me, O son of Pṛthā, as Ananta, Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, Hari, Śiva, / Brahmā, the Sun, Śeṣa, the all-pervading Lord. / To give you conviction, O son of Pṛthā, perceive that universal form of mine, / Supreme, meditated upon by yogins, which I showed you previously, O mighty-armed one.
Yudhiṣṭhira said: / [Tell me] the greatness and ritual procedure of the Ananta observance, O best of those who know ritual procedure; / what is its merit, what is its fruit, and what is its performance?
By whom was it previously performed, and by whom was it revealed in the world? / Explain all that at length, O Lord Nārāyaṇa.
The Blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / Formerly, in the Kṛta age, there lived a twice-born named Sumantu, / born in the lineage of Vasiṣṭha, learned, virtuous, and of subdued senses.
His wife was Dīkṣā, virtuous, devoted to vows of truth, / endowed with good conduct and character, beautiful, and born of the Bhṛgu lineage.
In the course of time a daughter possessing all auspicious marks was born to her; / named Śīlā, well-behaved, she grew up in her father's house.

4.94.s:

4.94.d:
माता तस्यास्तु कालेन ज्वरदाहप्रपीडिता ।
समागत्य नदीतोये मृता स्वर्गपुरं ययौ ॥
कृतं सुमन्तुना तस्याः कर्म्म यत् पारलौकिकं ।
ततः सुमन्तुः संत्यज्य दुःखं शोकं क्रमात् पुनः
नापत्नीको गृही धर्म्मं कर्त्तुमर्हति वै क्वचित् ।
इति सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा विवाहोत्सुकमानसः ॥
देवलस्य मुनेः कन्यां कर्कशां परिणीतवान् ।
सा कर्कशातिदुःशीला सदा निष्ठुरभाषिणी ॥
कोपना प्रतिकूला च निर्लज्जा कलहप्रिया ।
अदक्षा गृहृकृत्येषु दक्षा भोजनकर्म्मणि ॥
कलहेन तु सन्तुष्टा रुष्टा बन्धुजनान् प्रति ।
सा तु शीला पितुर्गेहे वर्द्धिता च दिने दिने ॥
करोति सखिभिः सार्द्धं शिशुक्रीडामनुत्तमां ।
गृहान्तरस्थलद्वारदेहलीतोरणादिषु ।
चतुरङ्गकवर्णैश्च रक्तपीतसितासितैः ।
स्वस्तिकं पद्मशङ्खौ च मण्डयन्ती पुनः पुनः ॥

4.94.s:
kurvvantī pratyahaṃ bālā devatātithipūjanaṃ .
gṛhakṛtye sadā dakṣā pituratyantavallabhā ..
kālena kiyatā viprastāṃ dṛṣṭvā yauvanodgatāṃ .

manasā cintayāmāsa sumantuḥ sutapāḥ sudhīḥ .
asmai bhāgyavaśācchīlā pratipādyā prayatnataḥ ..
iti kṛtvā matiṃ vipro dadau kanyāṃ śubhe dine .
kanyāmalaṅkṛtāṃ sādhvīṃ śīlāṃ candranibhānanāṃ ..
gṛhyoktavedavidhinā vivāhamakarottadā .
tato homādikaṃ karmma samāpya samaye muniḥ ..
4.94.d:
कुर्व्वन्ती प्रत्यहं बाला देवतातिथिपूजनं ।
गृहकृत्ये सदा दक्षा पितुरत्यन्तवल्लभा ॥
कालेन कियता विप्रस्तां दृष्ट्वा यौवनोद्गतां ।
कस्मै देया मया कन्या इति चिन्तान्वितोऽभवत्॥
ततो देववशात्तत्र कौण्डिन्यः समुपागतः ।
मुनिश्रेष्ठो महाभागः कुलीनो धर्मतत्परः ॥
मनसा चिन्तयामास सुमन्तुः सुतपाः सुधीः ।
अस्मै भाग्यवशाच्छीला प्रतिपाद्या प्रयत्नतः ॥
इति कृत्वा मतिं विप्रो ददौ कन्यां शुभे दिने ।
कन्यामलङ्कृतां साध्वीं शीलां चन्द्रनिभाननां ॥
गृह्योक्तवेदविधिना विवाहमकरोत्तदा ।
ततो होमादिकं कर्म्म समाप्य समये मुनिः ॥
4.94.m:
The maiden worshipped deities and guests every day; / ever skillful in household duties, she was extremely dear to her father.
After some time, seeing her arrived at youth, / the brahmin became anxious: 'To whom should I give my daughter?'
Then, by the force of destiny, Kauṇḍinya arrived there— / the best of sages, fortunate, of noble lineage, devoted to dharma.
Sumantu of good intellect and great asceticism thought in his mind: / 'By the power of fortune, Śīlā should be given to him with care.'
Having decided thus, on an auspicious day the brahmin gave his daughter, / the adorned, virtuous Śīlā whose face resembled the moon;
he performed the marriage according to the Vedic rites prescribed in the Gṛhyasūtras. / Then, having completed the oblations and other rites in due course, the sage

4.94.d:
सुमन्तुः कर्कशां प्राह जामात्रे देहि दक्षिणां
सफलं कुरु मे दानं प्रिये मुनिकुलोद्भवे ।
दक्षिणारहितं कर्म्म निष्फलं जायते यतः ।
सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कर्कशा कुपिताभवत् ।
सुमन्तुं भर्त्सयामास कर्कशैर्व्वचनैः पतिं ।
अलङ्कारं समानीय स्वकीयञ्चापि बन्धनं ॥
निक्षिप्य निभृते स्थाने कर्कशान्यगृहं ययौ ।
सुमन्तुश्चातिदीनात्मा लज्जितश्चाभवत्तदा ॥
यत्किञ्चिदर्थयोग्यञ्च द्रव्यमानीय यौतुकं ।
जामात्रे प्रददौ विप्रः परिचार्य्य पुनः पुनः ॥
ततो विवाहं निर्व्वर्त्य कौण्डिन्योऽपि निजाश्रमं ।
गोयाने तां समारोप्य शीलामादाय वै ययौ
ततः सा पथि गच्छन्ती शीला चन्द्रनिभानना
मध्याह्ने भोज्यवेलायां समुत्तीर्य्य सरित्तटे ॥
ददर्श शीला नारीणां समूहं व्रतचारिणां ।
पुंसां वृन्दञ्च तत्रेव रक्तपीताम्बरासनं ॥
4.94.m:
Sumantu said to Karkaśā: 'Give a sacrificial fee to the son-in-law; / make my gift fruitful, my dear one born of a sage's lineage, / for an act bereft of a sacrificial fee becomes fruitless.' / But upon hearing his words, Karkaśā became furious. / She rebuked her husband Sumantu with harsh words; / gathering up her ornaments and her valuables,
and putting them away in a secret place, Karkaśā went to another house. / Then Sumantu became very dejected and ashamed.
Bringing whatever trifling goods were suitable for a gift, / the brahmin gave them as a dowry to the son-in-law, attending upon him repeatedly.
Then, having concluded the wedding, Kauṇḍinya set out for his own hermitage, / placing Śīlā upon an ox-cart and taking her with him. / Then, travelling on the road, Śīlā, whose face resembled the moon, / alighted at midday at the time of eating on the bank of a river.
Śīlā saw a group of women performing a votive observance / and a company of men there, seated in red and yellow garments,

worshipping Ananta with devotion on the fourteenth day, individually. / Seeing the gathering of women, the virtuous woman asked respectfully;
bowing down with humility and prostrating before the Lord of gods, the virtuous lady [asked]: / 'What is this rite being performed by you ladies? Tell me that.'
The women said: / In the month of Bhādrapada, in the bright fortnight, when Indra's banner has been raised / and Mahendra has been worshipped upon poles in the shape of banners,
one who has bowed and bathed in a pool should begin the worship of Ananta, / fashioning the god out of darbha grass, accompanied by a vessel of water.
[One should invoke] Ananta, the Lord of the gods of gods, four-armed, wearing a diadem, / resembling an atasī flower, adorned with golden armlets,
holding conch, discus, mace, and the Śārṅga bow, bearing various weapons: / 'Come, come, Lord Kṛṣṇa, your sacrifice is proceeding.'
One should thus place the Lord Ananta upon the water vessel; / and offering flowers, food-offerings, incense, garments, and unguents upon the sacred circle,
one should worship Ananta, who is the universal form, with devotion. / For cakes, whatever is obtained of rice flour / or of barley and wheat,

एतेषां प्राप्यते यत्तु तद्ग्राह्यं प्रस्थसंज्ञितं ।
अर्द्धं विप्राय दातव्यमर्द्धमात्मनि योजयेत् ॥
पूजयित्वा तथा देवं गन्धपुष्पैर्यथाक्रमं ।
श्रुत्वा कथां ततस्तस्य कुङ्कमाक्तं सुडोरकं ॥
चतुर्दशग्रन्थियुक्तं नारी वामकरे न्यसेत् ।
पुमांस्तु दक्षिणे बाहौ तदानन्तं प्रपूजयेत् ॥
निर्व्वर्त्त्य पूजां देवस्य पूपं भुक्त्वा यथासुखं ।
विसृज्य दक्षिणां दत्त्वा प्रणम्य च यथासुखं ॥
शीला श्रुत्वा वचस्तासां यथा ताभिरुदाहृतं ।
व्रतं चकार सा बाहौ वद्धा डोरकमुत्तमं ।
पूपप्रस्थञ्च सा कृत्वा भुक्त्वा चैव तथैव च ।
4.94.m:

Having thus worshipped the god with perfumes and flowers in proper order, / and having then listened to his story, [taking] an excellent cord smeared with saffron,
tied with fourteen knots, a woman should tie it on her left hand / and a man on his right arm; then one should worship Ananta.
Having completed the worship of the god, having eaten the cake at pleasure, / having discharged [the deity], given the sacrificial fee, and bowed down with joy...
Hearing their words, just as it was related by them, / Śīlā performed the votive observance, tying the excellent cord upon her arm; / and having prepared a prastha of cakes, she ate it in that very manner.

4.94.d:
पुनर्जगाम तेनैव गोरथेन समन्विता ॥
तेनानन्तप्रसादेन गृहं गोधनसङ्कुलं ।
तदाश्रमं श्रिया युक्तं धनधान्यसमन्वितं ॥

दिव्याङ्गी शीलसम्पन्ना सावित्रीप्रतिमा यथा ॥

शीलोवाच ।
अनन्तं देवदेवस्य प्रमेयं डोरकं शुभं ।
करे बद्धं विधानेन शृणु मे वचनं प्रभो ॥
4.94.m:
She went on again together with that very ox-cart. / By that grace of Ananta, her house was crowded with cattle, / that hermitage was endowed with fortune and filled with wealth and grain, / crowded with various guests, adorned with various jewels, / and stocked with excellent horses, rutting elephants, buffaloes, and cattle. / And Śīlā, adorned with pearl ornaments and girdles of gems, / of celestial limbs and endowed with good character, was like an image of Sāvitrī. / Once she was seated, having come to the sacrificial fire-pit. / Kauṇḍinya too entered in anger, having seen the Ananta thread / tied carefully at the base of Śīlā's hand. / With angry words, his face crooked with knitted brows, he asked: / “Why do you remain here, wife, having tied this thread on your hand? / To what god is it an insignia? Tell me quickly, foolish woman!”
Śīlā said: / “The auspicious thread of Ananta, the god of gods, the insignia, / has been tied on my hand according to rule; hear my words, my lord.

4.94.d:
प्रसादाद् यस्य देवस्य भुङ्क्ते सुविपुलं धनं ।
न जानासि कथं नाथ तदेवं जगदीश्वरं ॥
शीलावाक्यं ततः श्रुत्वा कौण्डिन्यः कुपितोऽभवत् ।
कोऽसावनन्तसंज्ञो वै न श्रुतोऽपि वरानने ।
इत्युत्वाकृष्य कुपितो भुजाड्डोरमनन्तकं ।
क्षिप्तं ज्वालाकुले वह्नौ निर्भर्त्स्य बहुधा प्रियां ॥
ततः सा संभ्रमात् शीला हाहा कृत्वा प्रधाविता
वह्नेः सूत्रं समादाय क्षीरमध्ये ततोऽक्षिपत् ॥
ततस्तया करे वामे पुनर्बद्धं सुडोरकं ।
अनन्ताक्षेपदोषेण दारिद्र्यं पतितं गृहे ॥
न कैश्चित् वर्ण्यते लोकैः सोऽपि विप्रो युधिष्ठिर ।
गात्रे मलिनता प्राप्ता चक्षुर्निद्रां तथैव च ॥
शून्यानि गृहरूपाणि दग्धानि वह्निना क्वचित् ।
निरीक्ष्य स्वपुरं विप्रश्चिन्तयामास चेतसा ॥
अथ शीला विवर्णा सा दुःखिता पतिदोषतः।
विचचार पुरीं सर्व्वां शून्यागारसमन्वितां ॥
4.94.m:
By the grace of which god you enjoy abundant wealth— / how do you not know him, master, the lord of the universe in this manner?”
Then, having heard Śīlā's words, Kauṇḍinya became furious: / “Who indeed is this one called Ananta? He has not even been heard of, fair-faced woman!” / Saying this, enraged, he tore the Ananta thread from her arm, / cast it into the fire full of flames, and rebuked his beloved in many ways.
Then Śīlā, running forward in agitation crying “Alas, alas!”, / took the cord from the fire and threw it into the milk.
Then the fine thread was tied again by her on her left hand. / But through the fault of casting away Ananta, poverty fell upon the house.
That brāhmaṇa was not praised by any people, O Yudhiṣṭhira; / filthiness came upon his body, and his eyes were overcome with sleep.
The dwellings became empty, burnt by fire in places. / Beholding his own town, the brāhmaṇa reflected in his mind.
Then Śīlā, pale and sorrowful because of her husband's fault, / wandered through the whole city, which was filled with empty houses.

4.94.d:
अथ कौण्डिन्यविप्रस्य संजाता बुद्धिरुत्तमा ।
ममापि दुष्कृतं कर्म्म कृतं वा मे विगर्हितं ॥
अनन्ताक्षेपदोषेण ममापि गतिरीदृशी ।
अनन्तं यत्र पश्यामि तत्र यास्यामि दुर्मतिः ॥
ततो जगाम कौण्डिन्यो वनं व्याघ्रादिसङ्कुलं ।
व्रतस्यान्वेषणं कर्त्तुं पादौ द्रष्टुं तथा हरेः ॥
विह्वलः स ययौ मार्गे जनजन्तुविवर्ज्जिते ।
तत्रापश्यच्च तं वृक्षं फलपुष्पसमन्वितं ॥
वर्जितं पक्षिसङ्घातैः कीटैश्चैव विशेषतः ।
तमपृच्छत् त्वयानन्तः क्वचिद्दृष्टो महाद्रुम ॥
स चोवाच महावृक्षो नानन्तं वेद्मि भो द्विज
ततो गच्छन् ददर्शाग्रे तृणमध्ये सवत्सिकां ॥
तृणमध्ये प्रधावन्तो न खादति न जिघ्रति ।
हे महाधेनुके ब्रूहि किमनन्तस्त्वयेक्षितः ॥
सवत्सा तमुवाचाथ नानन्तं वेद्मि हे द्विज ।
ततो गच्छन् ददर्शाग्रे वृषश्रेष्ठं वने स्थितं ॥
4.94.m:
Then excellent understanding arose in the brāhmaṇa Kauṇḍinya: / “An evil deed was done by me, or a blameworthy act performed by me.
Through the fault of casting away Ananta, such is my condition too. / Wherever I may see Ananta, there I, evil-minded, will go.”
Then Kauṇḍinya went to the forest infested with tigers and other beasts, / in order to search for the votive observance and to behold the feet of Hari.
Distraught, he went along a path devoid of people or animals. / There he saw a tree endowed with fruits and flowers,
devoid of flocks of birds and especially of insects. / He asked it: “O great tree, have you seen Ananta anywhere?”
And that great tree said: “I do not know Ananta, O twice-born.” / Then, going on, he saw ahead [a cow] with her calf in the midst of grass.
Running in the midst of grass, she neither eats nor smells it. / “O great cow, tell me: was Ananta seen by you?”
She with her calf then said to him: “I do not know Ananta, O twice-born.” / Then, going on, he saw ahead an excellent bull standing in the forest.

4.94.d:
तमपृच्छदयं विप्रः अनन्तो वीक्षितस्त्वया ।
वृषभस्तमुवाचेदं विषण्णं ब्राह्मणं प्रति ॥
यद्यनन्तमहं जाने तदा मे गतिरीदृशी ।
ततो व्रजन् ददर्शाग्रे गर्दभं कुञ्जरं तथा ॥
नानामायाप्रचरन्तं मदगर्ज्जनदर्पितं ।
स तं दृष्ट्वा द्विजोऽपृच्छदनन्तं दृष्टवान् किमु ।
प्रत्युत्तरमुवाचेदं नानन्तं वेद्मि हे द्विज ।
ततो व्रजन् ददर्शाग्रे रम्यं पुष्करिणीद्वयं ॥
अन्योन्यजलसंघातैर्व्वीचिभिरुपशोभितं ।
शुभैः कुमुदकह्लारैः कमलोत्पलशोभितं ।
भ्रमरैश्चक्रवाकैश्च हंसकारण्डवैर्युतं ।
तमपृच्छत् द्विजोऽनन्तो भवतीभ्यञ्च लक्षितः ॥
पुष्करिण्यावूचतुस्तं न जानीवो हरिं क्वचित् ।
निपपात ततो विप्रो हाहा कृत्वा रुदन् भुवि ॥
किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि कथं पश्यामि तं विभुं ।
ततः कृपालु हृदयो देवेशो देवपूजितः ॥
4.94.m:
This brāhmaṇa asked him: “Was Ananta seen by you?” / The bull said this to the despondent brāhmaṇa:
“If I had known Ananta, then such would be my condition?” / Then, proceeding on, he saw ahead a donkey and an elephant,
wandering about with various illusions, arrogant with roaring in rut. / Having seen them, the twice-born asked: “Have you seen Ananta?” / They spoke this reply: “We do not know Ananta, O twice-born.” / Then, proceeding on, he saw ahead a delightful pair of lotus pools,
adorned with waves from the mutual surge of waters, / beautified with auspicious white water-lilies, night-lotuses, lotuses, and blue water-lilies, / filled with bees, cakravāka birds, geese, and kāraṇḍava ducks. / The twice-born asked them: “Has Ananta been noticed by you two?”
The two lotus pools said to him: “We do not know Hari anywhere.” / Then the brāhmaṇa fell to the earth, crying “Alas, alas!” and weeping:
“What shall I do? Where shall I go? How shall I see that all-pervading lord?” / Then the lord of gods, worshipped by the gods, compassionate at heart,

4.94.d:
तत्क्षणाद्भगवान् विष्णुर्द्विजप्रत्यक्षमागतः ।
वृद्धब्राह्मणरूपेण प्रोवाच वचनं द्विजं ॥
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ विप्रेन्द्र त्यज दुःखं सुखी भव ।
अनन्तं दर्शयिष्यामि कृष्णं विष्णुं हरिं शिवं ॥
ब्राह्मणं तं समादाय पातालवर्त्मना पुरीं ।
तां पुरीं दर्शयामास ततश्चान्तर्दधे द्विजः ।
स तां ददर्श कौण्डिन्यः पुरीं त्रैलोक्यदुर्ल्लभां
दिव्यनारीनरैर्युक्तां मणिरत्नविभूषितां ॥
सुवर्णरचितां सर्व्वां वेष्टितां तक्षकादिभिः ।
तत्रापश्यत् स कौण्डिन्यो देवदेवमनन्तकं ॥
विश्वरूपं जगन्नाथं चतुर्ब्बाहुं किरीटिनं ।
शङ्खचक्रगदापद्मधारिणं गरुडध्वजं ॥
दक्षिणे विलसल्लक्ष्मीं वामे क्रीडत्सरस्वतीं ।
सप्तफणासमायुक्तं दिव्यसिंहासनेस्थितं ।
एवं रूपं जगन्नाथं दृष्ट्वा भक्त्या स्तुतिः कृता ।
जगाम भूमौ शिरसा अनन्तस्य समीपतः ॥
4.94.m:
the blessed lord Viṣṇu, came in an instant before the eyes of the twice-born. / In the form of an old brāhmaṇa, he spoke these words to the twice-born:
“Arise, arise, O best of brāhmaṇas! Abandon your sorrow and be happy. / I shall show you Ananta, Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, Hari, Śiva.”
Taking that brāhmaṇa by the path of the netherworld to a city, / he showed him that city, and then the twice-born [guide] vanished. / Kauṇḍinya saw that city, difficult to attain in the three worlds, / filled with celestial women and men, adorned with pearls and jewels,
entirely made of gold, surrounded by Takṣaka and other serpents. / There Kauṇḍinya saw Ananta, the god of gods,
the universal-formed lord of the world, four-armed, crowned with a diadem, / bearing conch, discus, mace, and lotus, with Garuḍa on his banner,
with radiant Lakṣmī on his right and playful Sarasvatī on his left, / endowed with seven hoods, seated on a celestial throne. / Having seen the lord of the world of such form, he offered praise with devotion; / he went to the ground with his head bowed near Ananta:

4.94.d:
नमोऽस्त्वनन्ताय सहस्रमूर्त्तये सहस्रपादाक्षिशिरोरुबाहवे ।
सहस्रनाम्ने पुरुषाय शाश्वते सहस्रकोटीयुगधारिणे नमः ॥
अज्ञानेन मया देव यत् कृतं पापकर्मणा ।
तत्सर्व्वं कृपया शंस क्षमस्व मधुसूदन ॥ ॥
अथ कौण्डिन्यविप्रस्य स्तुतिं श्रुत्वा जनार्द्दनः ।
प्रसन्नो भगवान्देवश्चानन्तोऽनन्तरूपधृक् ॥
कथं मे प्रियमाख्यातमिहागच्छेति भूसुर ॥7 ॥
अनन्त उवाच ।
तुष्टोऽहं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठ भक्त्या तव विशेषतः ।
वरं गृहाण विप्रेन्द्र तुष्टोऽस्मि त्यज विस्मयं ॥
। कौण्डिन्य उवाच ।
स्वकर्म्मफलभोगेन यां यां योनिं व्रजाम्यहं ।
तस्यां तस्यां हृषीकेश हरिभक्तिर्दृढास्तु मे ॥
अतिप्रमादान्मोहाद्वा यन्मया दुष्कृतं कृतं ।
तदागः क्षम्यतां नाथ प्रणमामि पुनः पुनः ॥
श्रुत्वानन्तस्तु तद्वाक्यं ददौ तस्मै वरत्रयं ।
दारिद्रनाशनं धर्म्मं विष्णुलोकं तथाक्षयं .0॥
4.94.m:
“Homage to Ananta of a thousand forms, of a thousand feet, eyes, heads, thighs, and arms, / of a thousand names, the eternal person, the bearer of thousands of crores of yugas, homage!
Whatever has been done through ignorance by me, a sinner, / proclaim and forgive all that in mercy, O Madhusūdana!”
Then, having heard the praise of the brāhmaṇa Kauṇḍinya, Janārdana, / the gracious blessed lord, Ananta who bears infinite forms, [said:] / “How is it that what is dear to me has been declared? Come here, O brāhmaṇa!”
Ananta said:
I am pleased, O best of brāhmaṇas, especially with your devotion. / Choose a boon, O foremost of vipras; I am pleased, cast away your astonishment.
Kauṇḍinya said:
Into whatever womb I may enter through the experience of the fruit of my own deeds, / in that very [womb], O Hṛṣīkeśa, may my devotion to Hari remain steadfast!
Whatever misdeed I have committed out of excessive heedlessness or delusion, / may that offense be forgiven, O Lord! I bow down again and again.
Having heard his speech, Ananta gave him three boons: / the destruction of poverty, righteousness, and likewise the imperishable world of Viṣṇu.

4.94.s:

4.94.d:
कौण्डिन्य उवाच ।
पूर्णो मनोरथो देव मम चाद्य विशेषतः ।
किचित् पृच्छामि देवेश तन्मे ब्रूहि जगत्पते ॥
कश्चूतः को वृषः का गौः किन्तत् पुष्करिणीद्वयं ।
कः खरः कुञ्जरः को वा को वा वृद्धद्विजोत्तमः ।
कृपया कथयस्वाद्य पथि दृष्टो मया विभो ।
श्रीअनन्त उवाच ।
यश्चाम्रवृक्षो दृष्टो हि विप्रो विद्यासु गर्व्वितः ।
उपस्थिताय शिष्याय विद्यां यस्मान्न दत्तवान् ।
तेन कर्म्मविपाकेन वृक्षत्वं प्राप्य तिष्ठति ।
वृषभो यस्त्वया दृष्टो लोभकर्म्मकृतः पुरा ॥
दत्तं पर्य्युषितं द्रव्यं स्वादु भुक्तं स्वयं यतः ।
वृषभत्वं समासाद्य ततस्तिष्ठति निर्ज्जने ॥
विप्राय वसुधां दत्त्वा निष्फलां शस्यवर्ज्जितां ।
तेनासौ गोत्वमासाद्य तृणमध्ये प्रधावति ॥
धर्म्माधर्म्मौ विजानीयाद्यत्तत् पुष्करिणीद्वयं ।
गर्दभोऽज्ञानसम्पन्नः कुञ्जरो मदगर्वितः ॥
4.94.m:
Kauṇḍinya said:
My desire is fulfilled today, O God, especially; / I ask something, O Lord of gods; tell me that, O Lord of the universe!
What was the mango tree? What was the bull? What was the cow? What were those two lotus ponds? / What was the donkey, or what was the elephant, or who was that excellent old twice-born [man]? / Graciously tell me today, O omnipresent Lord, [whom] I saw along the path.
Śrī Ananta said:
The mango tree that was seen was indeed a vipra proud of his learning, / since he did not give his learning to a pupil who approached him. / By the fruition of that deed, he remains having obtained the condition of a tree. / The bull that was seen by you was formerly one who performed greedy deeds.
Because he gave stale goods and ate delicious [food] himself, / therefore, having attained the state of a bull, he stands in a lonely place.
Having given to a vipra land that was barren and devoid of crops, / by that [deed] he attained the state of a cow and runs about in the midst of grass.
One should know the two lotus ponds to be righteousness and unrighteousness. / The donkey was endowed with ignorance, [and] the elephant was proud with intoxication.

4.94.d:
ब्राह्मणोऽसावनन्तोऽहं यस्त्वया दर्शितो मुने ।
एतत्ते कथितं सर्व्वं गच्छ विप्र निजाश्रमं ॥
पुनः समृद्धिस्ते विप्र भविष्यति न संशयः ।
भुक्त्वा भोगांश्च विपुलान् संप्राप्स्यसि महत् पदं ॥
इति दत्त्वा वरं तस्मै तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ।
कौण्डिन्योऽयि गृहं गत्वा करोति व्रतमुत्तमं ॥
अनन्ताख्यं महापुण्यं वर्षाणाञ्च चतुर्दशं ।
शीलया सह धर्म्मात्मा सुखं भुक्त्वा मनोरथान् ॥
विष्णुरोकं समासाद्य रराज शीलया सह ।
अनन्ताख्यव्रतेनेह समाप्तेनैव पार्थिव ॥
सर्व्वपापविनिर्म्मुक्ता यास्यन्ति परमां गतिं ।
एवमेव हि नियमात् स्त्रियोऽनन्तव्रतान्नृप ॥
पुत्रपौत्रधनैर्युक्ता भुक्त्वा भोगान् मनोरथान् ।
विष्णुलोकमाप्नुवन्ति यावच्चन्द्रदिवाकरौ ॥
इति भविष्यपुराणे अनन्तव्रतं समाप्तं ।
श्रवणिकाव्रतम्
4.94.m:
That brāhmaṇa was I, Ananta, who showed himself to you, O sage. / All this has been told to you; go, O vipra, to your own hermitage.
Again you will have prosperity, O vipra, without a doubt. / Having enjoyed vast pleasures, you will attain the supreme abode.
Having given him the boon in this manner, he vanished right there. / Kauṇḍinya, too, having gone home, performs the excellent vrata,
greatly meritorious, named Ananta, for fourteen years, / together with Śīlā, the righteous-minded [sage] happily enjoying his desires.
Having reached the world of Viṣṇu, he shone together with Śīlā. / In this world, merely by completing the vrata named Ananta, O ruler of the earth,
freed from all sins, they will go to the supreme state. / In this very way, by the rule of the Anantavrata, O king, women,
endowed with sons, grandsons, and wealth, having enjoyed the pleasures of their desires, / attain the world of Viṣṇu as long as the moon and the sun [endure].
Thus ends the Anantavrata in the Bhaviṣyapurāṇa.
The Śravaṇikāvrata.

॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
विद्यंते देवताः पुण्याः श्रावण्यो नाम पांडव ॥
ब्रह्मणा प्रथमं सृष्टा नियोगश्च जने कृतः ॥ 2 ॥
4.95.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
There are meritorious deities named Śrāvaṇīs, O Pāṇḍava, / first created by Brahmā, and assigned among the people.

4.95.s:
yo yadvadati lokesmiñchubhaṃ vāpyatha vā'śubham ..
śrāvayaṃti hi tacchīghraṃ brāhmaṇyaḥ karmagocaram ..3..
4.95.d:
यो यद्वदति लोकेस्मिञ्छुभं वाप्यथ वाऽशुभम् ॥
श्रावयंति हि तच्छीघ्रं ब्राह्मण्यः कर्मगोचरम् ॥3॥
4.95.m: Whatever good or evil anyone says in this world, / those brāhmaṇas quickly cause [it], being within the range of action, to be heard.

4.95.s:
jātāstriloke pūjyāstu niyamena prajāpate ..
dūrācchravaṇavijñānaṃ dūrāddarśanagocaram ..4..
4.95.d:
जातास्त्रिलोके पूज्यास्तु नियमेन प्रजापते ॥
दूराच्छ्रवणविज्ञानं दूराद्दर्शनगोचरम् ॥4॥
4.95.m: They are born worthy of worship in the three worlds according to the ordinance, O lord of creatures; / their cognition of hearing is from afar, [and] their field of vision is from afar.

4.95.s:
tāsāmastīha sā śaktiracintyā tarkahetubhiḥ ..
naraistuṣṭaiśca yatproktaṃ kāryākāryasya kāraṇāt ..5..
4.95.d:
तासामस्तीह सा शक्तिरचिन्त्या तर्कहेतुभिः ॥
नरैस्तुष्टैश्च यत्प्रोक्तं कार्याकार्यस्य कारणात् ॥5॥
4.95.m: They possess in this world that power which is unthinkable through grounds of reasoning. / Whatever is spoken by pleased men on account of what should and should not be done,

4.95.s:
tacchṛṇvaṃti yataḥ pārtha naikā śrāvaṇikā matāḥ ..
yathā devā yathā daityā yathā vidyādharā narāḥ..6..
4.95.d:
तच्छृण्वंति यतः पार्थ नैका श्रावणिका मताः ॥
यथा देवा यथा दैत्या यथा विद्याधरा नराः॥6॥
4.95.m: since they hear that, O Pārtha, the Śrāvaṇikās are regarded as manifold. / Just as there are gods, daityas, vidyādharas, and men,

4.95.s:
yathā hi siddhagaṃdharvā nāgāḥ kiṃpuruṣāḥ khagāḥ..
rākṣasāśca piśācāśca devānāmaṣṭayonayaḥ..
tathaitāḥ puṇyanāmāno vaṃdyāḥ śrāvaṇikāḥ smṛtāḥ..7..
4.95.d:
यथा हि सिद्धगंधर्वा नागाः किंपुरुषाः खगाः॥
राक्षसाश्च पिशाचाश्च देवानामष्टयोनयः॥
तथैताः पुण्यनामानो वंद्याः श्रावणिकाः स्मृताः॥7॥
4.95.m: just as indeed there are siddhas, gandharvas, nāgas, kiṃpuruṣas, birds, / rākṣasas, and piśācas—the eight origins of the gods— / so these venerable [deities] of holy names are known as the Śrāvaṇikās.

4.95.s:
tā samuddiśya kartavyastaṃ nārīnarairiha ..
kiṃ tu tāsāṃ mahograṃ tu vrataṃ saṃyamanaṃ tadā ..8..
4.95.d:
ता समुद्दिश्य कर्तव्यस्तं नारीनरैरिह ॥
किं तु तासां महोग्रं तु व्रतं संयमनं तदा ॥8॥
4.95.m: Aiming at them, [this vrata] must be performed in this world by women and men; / but their vrata is very severe, and so is their restraint.

4.95.s:
āghrāya dhūpaṃ pakvānnaṃ jalaṃ cāgandha meva ca ..
dātavyā punaranyāsāṃ nārīṇāṃ bhojyapāraṇā ..9..
4.95.d:
आघ्राय धूपं पक्वान्नं जलं चागन्ध मेव च ॥
दातव्या पुनरन्यासां नारीणां भोज्यपारणा ॥9॥
4.95.m: Having smelled incense, cooked food, and water without fragrance, / the breaking of the fast with food must then be given to other women.

4.95.s:
adattvā yadi mṛtyuḥ syādaṃtarālepi pāṃḍava ..
tadā lagnagrahairgrastā lagnā hyuparikāraṭam ..
saphenilairmukhai raudrairbhriyaṃte nīcaduḥkhitāḥ .. 4.95.10 ..
4.95.d:
अदत्त्वा यदि मृत्युः स्यादंतरालेपि पांडव ॥
तदा लग्नग्रहैर्ग्रस्ता लग्ना ह्युपरिकारटम् ॥
सफेनिलैर्मुखै रौद्रैर्भ्रियंते नीचदुःखिताः ॥ 4.95.10 ॥
4.95.m: If death should occur even in the interval without having given [it], O Pāṇḍava, / then, seized by malignant planets and clinging above, / they die with frothing, dreadful mouths, miserable and degraded.

4.95.s:
śrūyaṃte hi purā pārtha pṛthivyāṃ nahuṣo nṛpaḥ ..
tasya bhāryā mahādevī jayaśrīrnāma bhārata .. 11 ..
4.95.d:
श्रूयंते हि पुरा पार्थ पृथिव्यां नहुषो नृपः ॥
तस्य भार्या महादेवी जयश्रीर्नाम भारत ॥ 11 ॥
4.95.m: Indeed, it is heard that formerly on earth, O Pārtha, there was a King Nahuṣa. / His chief queen, O Bhārata, was named Jayaśrī,

4.95.s:
pratyakṣarūpasaṃpannā darśanīyatarā śubhā ..
pīvarorustanā śyāmā mṛdukuñcitamūrddhajā .. 12 ..
4.95.d:
प्रत्यक्षरूपसंपन्ना दर्शनीयतरा शुभा ॥
पीवरोरुस्तना श्यामा मृदुकुञ्चितमूर्द्धजा ॥ 12 ॥
4.95.m: endowed with visible beauty, exceedingly lovely to look at, auspicious, / with plump thighs and breasts, dark-complexioned, with soft curly hair,

4.95.s:
śabdagadgadasaṃbhāṣā mattamātaṃgagāminī ..
yathārūpā tathā śīlā satī ceṣṭā mahītale .. 13 ..
4.95.d:
शब्दगद्गदसंभाषा मत्तमातंगगामिनी ॥
यथारूपा तथा शीला सती चेष्टा महीतले ॥ 13 ॥
4.95.m: speaking with faltering words, walking like an elephant in rut. / As was her beauty, so was her virtuous conduct, a faithful wife, beloved on the surface of the earth.

4.95.s:
sā kadācidgatā snātuṃ gaṃgāyāṃ cāśrame muneḥ ..
vaśiṣṭhasya dadarśātha satīṃ bhāryāmaruṃdhatīm .. 14 ..
4.95.d:
सा कदाचिद्गता स्नातुं गंगायां चाश्रमे मुनेः ॥
वशिष्ठस्य ददर्शाथ सतीं भार्यामरुंधतीम् ॥ 14 ॥
4.95.m: Once, having gone to bathe in the Gaṅgā and to the hermitage of the sage / Vasiṣṭha, she saw his virtuous wife, Arundhatī,

4.95.s:
bhojayaṃtī munīnāṃ tu patnīrnānānnabhojanaiḥ ..
tayā ca praṇipatyātha pṛṣṭā devyā mahāsatī .. 15 ..
4.95.d:
भोजयंती मुनीनां तु पत्नीर्नानान्नभोजनैः ॥
तया च प्रणिपत्याथ पृष्टा देव्या महासती ॥ 15 ॥
4.95.m: feeding the wives of the sages with various kinds of food. / And having bowed down to her, the great faithful wife was asked by the queen:

4.95.s: pūjyaṃ bhagavati brūhi kimetadvratamucyate .. 16 .. ..
4.95.d: पूज्यं भगवति ब्रूहि किमेतद्व्रतमुच्यते ॥ 16 ॥ ॥
4.95.m: O venerable lady, tell me what this worshipful vrata is called.

4.95.s:
.. arundhatyuvāca .. ..
jayaśriye śṛṇuṣva tvaṃ nāmnā śrāvaṇikāvratam..
etadbhartrā samākhyātaṃ vaśiṣṭhena maharṣiṇā..17..
4.95.d:
॥ अरुन्धत्युवाच ॥ ॥
जयश्रिये शृणुष्व त्वं नाम्ना श्रावणिकाव्रतम्॥
एतद्भर्त्रा समाख्यातं वशिष्ठेन महर्षिणा॥17॥
4.95.m:
Arundhatī said:
O Jayaśrī, listen to [the rite] named Śrāvaṇikāvrata; / this was fully declared by my husband, the great sage Vasiṣṭha.

4.95.s:
gūḍhaṃ bahmarṣisarvasvaṃ supativratakaṃ śubham ..
gaccha vā tiṣṭha vā rājñi tavātidhyaṃ karomyaham..18..
4.95.d:
गूढं बह्मर्षिसर्वस्वं सुपतिव्रतकं शुभम् ॥
गच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा राज्ञि तवातिध्यं करोम्यहम्॥18॥
4.95.m: It is secret, the all-in-all of the brāhmaṇa sages, bringing a good husband, auspicious. / Go or stay, O Queen, I shall extend hospitality to you.

4.95.s:
evamuktā jayaśrīstu bhojye tasminyadṛcchayā ..
bubhuje sāpi tatraiva aruṃdhatyā kṛtā darā .. 19 ..
4.95.d:
एवमुक्ता जयश्रीस्तु भोज्ये तस्मिन्यदृच्छया ॥
बुभुजे सापि तत्रैव अरुंधत्या कृता दरा ॥ 19 ॥
4.95.m: Having been spoken to thus, Jayaśrī, through spontaneous desire, / ate of that food right there, treated with respect by Arundhatī.

4.95.s:
bhuktvācamya jagāmātha svapuraṃ parameśvaram ..
kālena vismṛtaṃ tasyāstadvrataṃ tasya bhojanam .. 4.95.20 ..
4.95.d:
भुक्त्वाचम्य जगामाथ स्वपुरं परमेश्वरम् ॥
कालेन विस्मृतं तस्यास्तद्व्रतं तस्य भोजनम् ॥ 4.95.20 ॥
4.95.m: Having eaten and sipped water, she went to her own supreme city. / With time, that vrata and the meal of it were forgotten by her.

4.95.s:
tatastu samaye pūrṇe mriyamāṇā mahāsatī ..
jayaśrīrghargharaṃ gaṃtuṃ kurvāṇā kaṃṭhagadgadam .. 21 ..
4.95.d:
ततस्तु समये पूर्णे म्रियमाणा महासती ॥
जयश्रीर्घर्घरं गंतुं कुर्वाणा कंठगद्गदम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.95.m: Then, when her time was complete, dying, the great faithful wife / Jayaśrī made a rattling sound, choked in her throat,

4.95.s:
phenaṃ lālāvilādvaktrādudgiraṃtī muhurmuhuḥ ..
sthitā paṃcadaśāhāni bībhatsā dāruṇānanā .. 22 ..
4.95.d:
फेनं लालाविलाद्वक्त्रादुद्गिरंती मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
स्थिता पंचदशाहानि बीभत्सा दारुणानना ॥ 22 ॥
4.95.m: emitting foam again and again from her mouth smeared with saliva; / she remained for fifteen days, repulsive, with a terrifying face.

4.95.s:
tataḥ ṣoḍaśake prāpte dine svayamaruṃdhatī ..
praviśyābhyaṃtaraṃ pūrṇaṃ tāṃ rājñīmavalokya ca ..
nahuṣāya samācakhyau yaduktaṃ śrāvaṇī vrate .. 23 ..
4.95.d:
ततः षोडशके प्राप्ते दिने स्वयमरुंधती ॥
प्रविश्याभ्यंतरं पूर्णं तां राज्ञीमवलोक्य च ॥
नहुषाय समाचख्यौ यदुक्तं श्रावणी व्रते ॥ 23 ॥
4.95.m: Then, when the sixteenth day arrived, Arundhatī herself / entered into the inner chamber and, having beheld that queen, / related to Nahuṣa what was prescribed in the Śrāvaṇī-vrata.

4.95.s:
tacchutvā nahuṣo rājā drutaṃ bhojyaṃ pracakrame ..
yathoktaṃ tadaruṃdhatyā yacca yāvadabhīpsitam .. 24 ..
4.95.d:
तच्छुत्वा नहुषो राजा द्रुतं भोज्यं प्रचक्रमे ॥
यथोक्तं तदरुंधत्या यच्च यावदभीप्सितम् ॥ 24 ॥
4.95.m: Having heard that, King Nahuṣa quickly set about [giving] food, / exactly as had been spoken by Arundhatī, whatever and as much as was desired.

4.95.s:
datvā ca karakānaṣṭau tāmuddiśya jayaśriyam ..
kṣaṇājjagāma pañcatvaṃ karakāṇāṃ pradānataḥ .. 25 ..
4.95.d:
दत्वा च करकानष्टौ तामुद्दिश्य जयश्रियम् ॥
क्षणाज्जगाम पञ्चत्वं करकाणां प्रदानतः ॥ 25 ॥
4.95.m:
And having given eight water-pitchers dedicated to that Jayasrī,
she attained death in an instant from the gift of the water-pitchers.

4.95.s:
jagāma śakralokaṃ sā vimānenārkavarcasā ..
dodhūyamānā camaraiḥ stūyamānā surā suraiḥ .. 26 ..
4.95.d:
जगाम शक्रलोकं सा विमानेनार्कवर्चसा ॥
दोधूयमाना चमरैः स्तूयमाना सुरा सुरैः ॥ 26 ॥
4.95.m:
She went to Indra's world in a celestial chariot brilliant as the sun,
fanned by chowries and praised by gods and asuras.

4.95.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
mārgaśīrṣādimāseṣu dvādaśasvapi pāṃḍava ..
dravyaprāptiśca bhaktiśca dānakāle praśasyate .. 27 ..
4.95.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
मार्गशीर्षादिमासेषु द्वादशस्वपि पांडव ॥
द्रव्यप्राप्तिश्च भक्तिश्च दानकाले प्रशस्यते ॥ 27 ॥
4.95.m:
Lord Kṛṣṇa said:
In all twelve months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa, O son of Pāṇḍu,
the acquisition of wealth and devotion are praised at the time of giving.

4.95.s:
bhuktvā yajñe caturdaśyāmaṣṭamyāṃ vā yudhiṣṭhira ..
vratī snātvā tu pūrvāhṇe nadyādau vimale jale .. 28 ..
4.95.d:
भुक्त्वा यज्ञे चतुर्दश्यामष्टम्यां वा युधिष्ठिर ॥
व्रती स्नात्वा तु पूर्वाह्णे नद्यादौ विमले जले ॥ 28 ॥
4.95.m:
Having eaten at a sacrifice on the fourteenth or on the eighth, O Yudhiṣṭhira,
the observer of the votive observance, having bathed in the morning in clear water such as a river,

4.95.s:
āmaṃtrayeddaśaikaikā nārīrgaurīsvarūpiṇīḥ ..
yatācārāḥ suveṣāśca brāhmaṇīrvā svagotrajāḥ .. 29 ..
4.95.d:
आमंत्रयेद्दशैकैका नारीर्गौरीस्वरूपिणीः ॥
यताचाराः सुवेषाश्च ब्राह्मणीर्वा स्वगोत्रजाः ॥ 29 ॥
4.95.m:
should invite ten individual women who embody Gaurī,
of restrained conduct and fine dress, or Brahmin women born of his own lineage;

4.95.s:
dvādaśa brāhmaṇāṃstatra vedavedāṃgapāragān ..
maṃtrajñānitihāsajñānupaśāṃtāñjitendriyān .. 4.95.30 ..
4.95.d:
द्वादश ब्राह्मणांस्तत्र वेदवेदांगपारगान् ॥
मंत्रज्ञानितिहासज्ञानुपशांताञ्जितेन्द्रियान् ॥ 4.95.30 ॥
4.95.m:
and there twelve Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
knowers of mantras, knowers of the Itihāsas, tranquil and self-controlled.

4.95.s:
sarvaṃ dadyādvidhānena pādakṣālanapūrvakam ..
caṃdanena sugandhena puṣpadhūpādinā tathā .. 31 ..
4.95.d:
सर्वं दद्याद्विधानेन पादक्षालनपूर्वकम् ॥
चंदनेन सुगन्धेन पुष्पधूपादिना तथा ॥ 31 ॥
4.95.m:
He should offer everything according to rule, preceded by washing their feet,
with fragrant sandalwood, flowers, incense, and the like;

4.95.s:
grīvāsūtrakasiṃdūrakuṃkumena ca bhūṣayet ..
tāsāmagre pradātavyā varddhanyo dvādaśaiva tu .. 32 ..
4.95.d:
ग्रीवासूत्रकसिंदूरकुंकुमेन च भूषयेत् ॥
तासामग्रे प्रदातव्या वर्द्धन्यो द्वादशैव तु ॥ 32 ॥
4.95.m:
and he should adorn them with necklaces, red lead, and saffron.
Twelve vardhanī vessels should be given before them,

4.95.s:
acchidrā jalapūrṇāstu suvṛttāḥ sūtraveṣṭitāḥ ..
sohālakādibhiścchannāḥ puṣpamālāvibhūṣitāḥ .. 33 ..
4.95.d:
अच्छिद्रा जलपूर्णास्तु सुवृत्ताः सूत्रवेष्टिताः ॥
सोहालकादिभिश्च्छन्नाः पुष्पमालाविभूषिताः ॥ 33 ॥
4.95.m:
flawless, filled with water, well-rounded, wrapped with cord,
covered with sohālaka pastries and the like, adorned with garlands of flowers,

4.95.s:
caṃdanena samālabdhāḥ sahiraṇyāḥ pṛthakpṛthak ..
tanmadhye varddhanīṃ caikāṃ svake śīrṣe niveśayet .. 34 ..
4.95.d:
चंदनेन समालब्धाः सहिरण्याः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
तन्मध्ये वर्द्धनीं चैकां स्वके शीर्षे निवेशयेत् ॥ 34 ॥
4.95.m:
smeared with sandalwood, each individually accompanied by gold.
And among them he should place one vardhanī vessel upon his own head.

4.95.s:
sthitvā maṇḍalake madhye yajamānaḥ svayaṃ tadā ..
yadbālye yacca kaumāre vārddhake vāpi yatkṛtam ..
tatsarvaṃ nāśamāyātu pitṛdevarṣiṇāṃ nṛṇām .. 35 ..
4.95.d:
स्थित्वा मण्डलके मध्ये यजमानः स्वयं तदा ॥
यद्बाल्ये यच्च कौमारे वार्द्धके वापि यत्कृतम् ॥
तत्सर्वं नाशमायातु पितृदेवर्षिणां नृणाम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.95.m:
Standing then in the center of the diagram, the patron of the rite himself [should say]:
'Whatever has been done in childhood, youth, or old age,
may all that perish, of the ancestors, gods, seers, and men.

4.95.s:
imā me samayaṃ svarṇaṃ tārayasva bhavārṇavāt ..
adyāhaṃ gantumicchāmi viṣṇoḥ padamanuttamam ..
evamastviti tā brūyuḥ striyaḥ sarvā yudhiṣṭhira .. 36 ..
4.95.d:
इमा मे समयं स्वर्णं तारयस्व भवार्णवात् ॥
अद्याहं गन्तुमिच्छामि विष्णोः पदमनुत्तमम् ॥
एवमस्त्विति ता ब्रूयुः स्त्रियः सर्वा युधिष्ठिर ॥ 36 ॥
4.95.m:
Keep this covenant of mine with gold; carry [me] across the ocean of worldly existence.
Today I desire to go to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.'
'May it be so,' all those women should say, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

4.95.s:
tato brāhmaṇamāhūya yajamāna idaṃ vadet ..
brūhi brāhmaṇa yanme tvamaghaṃ yena kṣayaṃ vrajet .. 37 ..
4.95.d:
ततो ब्राह्मणमाहूय यजमान इदं वदेत् ॥
ब्रूहि ब्राह्मण यन्मे त्वमघं येन क्षयं व्रजेत् ॥ 37 ॥
4.95.m:
Then, having summoned a Brahmin, the patron of the rite should say this:
'Tell me, Brahmin, that through which my sin may be destroyed.

4.95.s:
uttīrya śrāvaṇaṃ māsaṃ samuttāraya sāṃpratam ..
uttārayeta maṃtreṇa brāhmaṇo vardhanī ca tām .. 38 ..
4.95.d:
उत्तीर्य श्रावणं मासं समुत्तारय सांप्रतम् ॥
उत्तारयेत मंत्रेण ब्राह्मणो वर्धनी च ताम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.95.m:
Having crossed over the month of Śrāvaṇa, now carry [me] completely across.'
The Brahmin should remove that vardhanī vessel with the mantra:

4.95.s:
upoṣya śiraso devyāḥ samuttīrya ruhadrumān ..
kaṭukaṃ niṃbavṛkṣaṃ vā tato madhukamāruha ..
tato gaccha mahādevaṃ śravaṇe śravaṇottame .. 39 .. iti vardhanikottāraṇamantraḥ ..
4.95.d:
उपोष्य शिरसो देव्याः समुत्तीर्य रुहद्रुमान् ॥
कटुकं निंबवृक्षं वा ततो मधुकमारुह ॥
ततो गच्छ महादेवं श्रवणे श्रवणोत्तमे ॥ 39 ॥ इति वर्धनिकोत्तारणमन्त्रः ॥
4.95.m:
'Having fasted, crossing over the ascending trees from the goddess's head,
either the bitter nimba tree, then climb the madhuka;
then go to Mahādeva on Śravaṇa, the best of the Śravaṇa asterisms.'
Thus is the mantra for removing the vardhanī vessel.

4.95.s: evaṃ tāḥ samayaṃ procya dattvāśīrvacanāni ca ..4.95.40..
4.95.d: एवं ताः समयं प्रोच्य दत्त्वाशीर्वचनानि च ॥4.95.40॥
4.95.m: Having thus declared the covenant to them and given words of blessing,

4.95.s:
tāṃ varddhanikāmekānte viprāya pratipādayet ..
gṛhītvā karakānnāryyo vrajeyuḥ sveṣu veśmasu .. 41 ..
4.95.d:
तां वर्द्धनिकामेकान्ते विप्राय प्रतिपादयेत् ॥
गृहीत्वा करकान्नार्य्यो व्रजेयुः स्वेषु वेश्मसु ॥ 41 ॥
4.95.m:
he should present that vardhanī vessel to the Brahmin in private.
Taking the water-pitchers, the women should depart to their own homes.

4.95.s:
yajamāno'pi yātāsu yatheṣṭaṃ kāmamācaret ..
evamācarate pārtha śrāvaṇīvrata mādarāt ..42..
4.95.d:
यजमानोऽपि यातासु यथेष्टं काममाचरेत् ॥
एवमाचरते पार्थ श्रावणीव्रत मादरात् ॥42॥
4.95.m:
When they have gone, the patron of the rite may act according to his desire.
Whoever thus observes with respect the Śrāvaṇī-vrata, O son of Pṛthā,

4.95.s:
tasya kāle tu saṃprāpte sukhaṃ mṛtyuḥ prajāyate ..
nirvyādhirnīrujo bhogī sthitvāsthitvā śataṃ sukham .. 43 ..
4.95.d:
तस्य काले तु संप्राप्ते सुखं मृत्युः प्रजायते ॥
निर्व्याधिर्नीरुजो भोगी स्थित्वास्थित्वा शतं सुखम् ॥ 43 ॥
4.95.m:
for him, when the time arrives, an easy death occurs.
Free of disease, without illness, enjoying pleasures, after living happily for a hundred [years],

4.95.s:
putrapautrasamṛddhyādau bhuktvā martyasukhāni ca ..
rudralokamavāpnoti somalokaṃ sa gacchati .. 44 ..
4.95.d:
पुत्रपौत्रसमृद्ध्यादौ भुक्त्वा मर्त्यसुखानि च ॥
रुद्रलोकमवाप्नोति सोमलोकं स गच्छति ॥ 44 ॥
4.95.m:
having enjoyed mortal pleasures in the prosperity of sons and grandsons and so forth,
he attains Rudra's world and goes to Soma's world.

4.95.s:
strīṇāṃ tulyaṃ sa hīno'pi vratī vrataphalaṃ vrajet ..
gaurībhojyeṣu datteṣu ekādaśasu yatphalam .. 45 ..
4.95.d:
स्त्रीणां तुल्यं स हीनोऽपि व्रती व्रतफलं व्रजेत् ॥
गौरीभोज्येषु दत्तेषु एकादशसु यत्फलम् ॥ 45 ॥
4.95.m:
Even a low person observing the votive observance attains the fruit of the observance equal to women.
Whatever fruit comes when eleven feasts of Gaurī are given,

4.95.s:
tadekenāpi labhate pārtha śrāvaṇikāvrate ..
bhaktyā gacchaṃti te lokānvihṛtya sukhamādarāt .. 46 .. ..
śrīkṛṣṇayudhiṣṭhirasaṃvādavarṇanam
4.95.d:
तदेकेनापि लभते पार्थ श्रावणिकाव्रते ॥
भक्त्या गच्छंति ते लोकान्विहृत्य सुखमादरात् ॥ 46 ॥ ॥
श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवादवर्णनम्
4.95.m:
one obtains that even through a single [observance] in the Śrāvaṇikā-vrata, O son of Pṛthā.
With devotion they go to those worlds, sporting happily and with honor.
Description of the Dialogue Between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira

4.96.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
atha naktopavāsasya vidhānaṃ śṛṇu pāṃḍava ..
yena vijñātamātreṇa naro mokṣamavāpnuyāt .. 1 ..
4.96.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
अथ नक्तोपवासस्य विधानं शृणु पांडव ॥
येन विज्ञातमात्रेण नरो मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 1 ॥
4.96.m:
Lord Kṛṣṇa said:
Now hear the procedure for the nocturnal fast, O son of Pāṇḍu,
by merely knowing which a man may attain liberation.

4.96.s:
yeṣu teṣu ca māseṣu śuklapakṣe caturdaśīm ..
brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayitvā tu prārabheta tato vratam .. 2 ..
4.96.d:
येषु तेषु च मासेषु शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्दशीम् ॥
ब्राह्मणं भोजयित्वा तु प्रारभेत ततो व्रतम् ॥ 2 ॥
4.96.m:
On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight in any of the months,
having fed a Brahmin, he should then begin the votive observance.

4.96.s:
māsimāsi bhavaṃti dvāvaṣṭamyau ca caturdaśī ..
śivārcanarato bhūtvā śivadhyānaikamānasaḥ ..
vasudhābhājanaṃ kṛtvā bhuñjīyānnaktabhojanam .. 3 ..
4.96.d:
मासिमासि भवंति द्वावष्टम्यौ च चतुर्दशी ॥
शिवार्चनरतो भूत्वा शिवध्यानैकमानसः ॥
वसुधाभाजनं कृत्वा भुञ्जीयान्नक्तभोजनम् ॥ 3 ॥
4.96.m:
In every month there are two eighth days and a fourteenth.
Devoted to the worship of Śiva, his mind solely fixed in meditation on Śiva,
using the earth as his dish, he should eat the nocturnal meal.

4.96.s:
upavāsātparaṃ bhaikṣyaṃ bhaikṣyātparamayācitam ..
ayācitātparaṃ naktaṃ tasmānnaktena bhojayet .. 4 ..
4.96.d:
उपवासात्परं भैक्ष्यं भैक्ष्यात्परमयाचितम् ॥
अयाचितात्परं नक्तं तस्मान्नक्तेन भोजयेत् ॥ 4 ॥
4.96.m:
Begged food is superior to fasting; unasked-for food is superior to begged food;
the nocturnal meal is superior to unasked-for food; therefore he should feed with the nocturnal meal.

4.96.s:
devaiśca bhuktaṃ pūrvāhṇe madhyāhne munibhistathā ..
aparāhṇe ca pitṛbhiḥ sandhyāyāṃ guhyakādibhiḥ .. 5 ..
4.96.d:
देवैश्च भुक्तं पूर्वाह्णे मध्याह्ने मुनिभिस्तथा ॥
अपराह्णे च पितृभिः सन्ध्यायां गुह्यकादिभिः ॥ 5 ॥
4.96.m:
The gods eat in the forenoon, and likewise the sages at midday,
the ancestors in the afternoon, and the guhyakas and others at twilight.

4.96.s:
sarvalokānatikramya naktabhojī sadā bhavet ..
haviṣya bhojanaṃ snānaṃ satyamāhāralāghavam .. 6 ..
4.96.d:
सर्वलोकानतिक्रम्य नक्तभोजी सदा भवेत् ॥
हविष्य भोजनं स्नानं सत्यमाहारलाघवम् ॥ 6 ॥
4.96.m:
Transcending all beings, one should always eat only at night.
Eating sacrificial food, bathing, truthfulness, lightness of diet,

4.96.s:
agnikāryo hyadhaḥśayyo naktabhojī sadā bhavet ..
evaṃ saṃvatsarasyāṃte vratapūrṇasya sarpiṣā ..
pūrṇakumbhoparisthāpya pūjayecca suśobhane .. 7 ..
4.96.d:
अग्निकार्यो ह्यधःशय्यो नक्तभोजी सदा भवेत् ॥
एवं संवत्सरस्यांते व्रतपूर्णस्य सर्पिषा ॥
पूर्णकुम्भोपरिस्थाप्य पूजयेच्च सुशोभने ॥ 7 ॥
4.96.m:
tending the sacred fire, sleeping on the ground—he should always be an eater of the nocturnal meal.
Thus at the end of a year of the completed votive observance, with clarified butter
placed upon a full water-jar, he should worship [Śiva], O fair one.

4.96.s:
kapilāpañcagavyena sthāpayenmṛnmayaṃ śivam ..
phalaṃ puṣpaṃ yavakṣīraṃ dadhi dūrvāṃkurāṃstathā ..8 ..
4.96.d:
कपिलापञ्चगव्येन स्थापयेन्मृन्मयं शिवम् ॥
फलं पुष्पं यवक्षीरं दधि दूर्वांकुरांस्तथा ॥8 ॥
4.96.m:
With the five products of a brown cow he should install an earthen Śiva.
Fruit, flowers, barley with milk, curd, and sprouts of dūrvā grass,

4.96.s:
tatkumbhānāṃ jalonmiśramarghamaṣṭāṃgamucyate ..
śirasā dhārayitvā tu jānū kṛtvā mahītale .. 9 ..
4.96.d:
तत्कुम्भानां जलोन्मिश्रमर्घमष्टांगमुच्यते ॥
शिरसा धारयित्वा तु जानू कृत्वा महीतले ॥ 9 ॥
4.96.m:
mixed with the water of those jars, is called the eightfold guest-offering.
Bearing it upon his head, placing both knees upon the surface of the earth,

4.96.s:
mahādevāya dātavyaṃ gandhapuṣpaṃ yathākramam ..
bhakṣyodenairbaliṃ kṛtvā praṇamya parameśvarīm .. 4.96.10 ..
4.96.d:
महादेवाय दातव्यं गन्धपुष्पं यथाक्रमम् ॥
भक्ष्योदेनैर्बलिं कृत्वा प्रणम्य परमेश्वरीम् ॥ 4.96.10 ॥
4.96.m:
he should offer perfume and flowers in due order to Mahādeva.
Having made an offering with edible grains and bowed to Parameśvarī,

4.96.s:
dhenuṃ vā dakṣiṇāṃ dadyādvṛṣaṃ vāpi dhuraṃdharam ..
śrotriyāya daridrāya kalpavratavidāya ca ..
yo dadāti śive bhaktyā tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 11 ..
4.96.d:
धेनुं वा दक्षिणां दद्याद्वृषं वापि धुरंधरम् ॥
श्रोत्रियाय दरिद्राय कल्पव्रतविदाय च ॥
यो ददाति शिवे भक्त्या तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥ 11 ॥
4.96.m:
he should give as a priestly fee a cow or a draft ox
to a poor Brahmin learned in the Veda who knows the ritual of votive observances.
Hear the meritorious fruit of him who gives with devotion to Śiva:

4.96.s:
vimānamarkapratimaṃ haṃsayuktamalaṃkṛtam..
ārūḍho'psarasāṃ gītairyāti rudrālaye sukham .. 12 ..
4.96.d:
विमानमर्कप्रतिमं हंसयुक्तमलंकृतम्॥
आरूढोऽप्सरसां गीतैर्याति रुद्रालये सुखम् ॥ 12 ॥
4.96.m:
Mounted on a celestial chariot resembling the sun, adorned and drawn by swans,
he goes happily to Rudra's abode accompanied by the songs of apsarases.

4.96.s:
sthitvā rudrasya bhavane varṣakoṭiśatatrayam ..
iha loke nṛpaśreṣṭha grāmalakṣeśvaro bhavet .. 13 ..
4.96.d:
स्थित्वा रुद्रस्य भवने वर्षकोटिशतत्रयम् ॥
इह लोके नृपश्रेष्ठ ग्रामलक्षेश्वरो भवेत् ॥ 13 ॥
4.96.m:
Remaining in Rudra's mansion for three hundred crores of years,
he becomes the lord of a hundred thousand villages in this world, O best of kings.

4.96.s:
yaścāṣṭamīṣu ca śivāsu caturdaśīṣu naktaṃ samācarati śāstravidhāna dṛṣṭam ..
svargāṃganākalaravākulitaṃ vimānamāruhya yāti sa sukhena sureśalokam .. 14 .. ..
śivacaturdaśīvratavarṇanam
4.96.d:
यश्चाष्टमीषु च शिवासु चतुर्दशीषु नक्तं समाचरति शास्त्रविधान दृष्टम् ॥
स्वर्गांगनाकलरवाकुलितं विमानमारुह्य याति स सुखेन सुरेशलोकम् ॥ 14 ॥ ॥
शिवचतुर्दशीव्रतवर्णनम्
4.96.m:
And he who observes the nocturnal meal on the auspicious eighth and fourteenth days according to the prescription of the scriptures,
mounting a celestial chariot filled with the sweet murmur of celestial maidens, goes happily to the world of the lord of the gods.
Description of the Śivacaturdaśī-vrata

4.97.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājanvakṣye māheśvaraṃ vratam ..
triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṃ nāmnā śivacaturdaśī .. 1 ..
4.97.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
शृणुष्वावहितो राजन्वक्ष्ये माहेश्वरं व्रतम् ॥
त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं नाम्ना शिवचतुर्दशी ॥ 1 ॥
4.97.m:
Lord Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen attentively, O king; I shall explain the votive observance of Maheśvara,
renowned in the three worlds by the name Śivacaturdaśī.

4.97.s:
mārgaśīrṣatrayodaśyāṃ sitāyāmekabhuṅnaraḥ ..
māseṣvanyeṣu vā rājanpārtha evaṃ na kārayet .. 2 ..
4.97.d:
मार्गशीर्षत्रयोदश्यां सितायामेकभुङ्नरः ॥
मासेष्वन्येषु वा राजन्पार्थ एवं न कारयेत् ॥ 2 ॥
4.97.m:
A man should eat only once on the bright thirteenth of Mārgaśīrṣa;
in other months, O king, O son of Pṛthā, he should not do so.

4.97.s:
caturdaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ samabhyarcya maheśvaram ..
sauvarṇaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ dattvā bhakṣyāmi ca pare'hani.. 3 ..
4.97.d:
चतुर्दश्यां निराहारः समभ्यर्च्य महेश्वरम् ॥
सौवर्णं वृषभं दत्त्वा भक्ष्यामि च परेऽहनि॥ 3 ॥
4.97.m: "Fasting without food on the fourteenth day, having worshipped Maheśvara, / and having given a golden bull, I will eat on the next day."

4.97.s:
evaṃ niyamakṛtsuptvā prātarutthāya mānavaḥ ..
kṛtasnānajapaḥ paścādumayā saha śaṃkaram ..
pūjayetkusumaiḥ śuklairgaṃdhadhūpānulepanaiḥ .. 4 ..
4.97.d:
एवं नियमकृत्सुप्त्वा प्रातरुत्थाय मानवः ॥
कृतस्नानजपः पश्चादुमया सह शंकरम् ॥
पूजयेत्कुसुमैः शुक्लैर्गंधधूपानुलेपनैः ॥ 4 ॥
4.97.m: Having made such a resolve and slept, waking up in the morning, a man, / having performed his bath and muttered prayers, should afterwards worship Śaṅkara along with Umā / with white flowers, fragrances, incenses, and ointments.

4.97.s:
pādau namaḥ śivāyeti śiraḥ sarvātmane namaḥ ..
lalāṭaṃ tu trinetrāya netrāṇi haraye namaḥ .. 5 ..
4.97.d:
पादौ नमः शिवायेति शिरः सर्वात्मने नमः ॥
ललाटं तु त्रिनेत्राय नेत्राणि हरये नमः ॥ 5 ॥
4.97.m: [He should worship] the feet with "Homage to Śiva"; the head with "Homage to the Soul of All"; / the forehead indeed with "[Homage] to the Three-Eyed One"; the eyes with "Homage to Hara";

4.97.s:
mukhamindumukhāyeti tatheśānāya codaram ..
pārśve cānaṃtadharmāya jñānarūpāya vai kaṭim .. 6 ..
4.97.d:
मुखमिन्दुमुखायेति तथेशानाय चोदरम् ॥
पार्श्वे चानंतधर्माय ज्ञानरूपाय वै कटिम् ॥ 6 ॥
4.97.m: the face with "[Homage] to the Moon-faced One"; likewise the belly with "[Homage] to Īśāna"; / the two flanks with "[Homage] to Infinite Virtue"; and the waist with "[Homage] to the Embodiment of Knowledge";

4.97.s:
ūrū cānantyavairāgyaṃ jānunī cārcayedbudhaḥ ..
pradhānāya namo jaṃghe gulphau vyomātmane namaḥ .. 7 ..
4.97.d:
ऊरू चानन्त्यवैराग्यं जानुनी चार्चयेद्बुधः ॥
प्रधानाय नमो जंघे गुल्फौ व्योमात्मने नमः ॥ 7 ॥
4.97.m: and the wise man should worship the thighs with "[Homage to] Infinite Dispassion" and the two knees; / the shanks with "Homage to Pradhāna"; the ankles with "Homage to the Sky-souled One";

4.97.s:
vyomavyomātmarūpāya pṛṣṭhamabhyarcayennaraḥ ..
namaḥ sṛṣṭyai namastuṣṭyai pārvatīṃ cāpi pūjayet .. 8 ..
4.97.d:
व्योमव्योमात्मरूपाय पृष्ठमभ्यर्चयेन्नरः ॥
नमः सृष्ट्यै नमस्तुष्ट्यै पार्वतीं चापि पूजयेत् ॥ 8 ॥
4.97.m: a man should worship the back with "[Homage] to the Embodiment of the Sky and of the Nature of Sky." / He should also worship Pārvatī with "Homage to Sṛṣṭi, homage to Tuṣṭi!"

4.97.s:
tataśca vṛṣabhaṃ haimamudakumbhasamanvitam ..
śuklamālyāṃbarayutaṃ pañcaratnavibhūṣitam .. 9 ..
4.97.d:
ततश्च वृषभं हैममुदकुम्भसमन्वितम् ॥
शुक्लमाल्यांबरयुतं पञ्चरत्नविभूषितम् ॥ 9 ॥
4.97.m: Then, a golden bull accompanied by a water-pot, / provided with white garlands and garments, adorned with five jewels,

4.97.s:
bhakṣyairnānāvidhairyuktaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet ..
prīyatāṃ devadevo'tra sadyojātaḥ pinākadhṛk.. 4.97.10 ..
4.97.d:
भक्ष्यैर्नानाविधैर्युक्तं ब्राह्मणाय निवेदयेत् ॥
प्रीयतां देवदेवोऽत्र सद्योजातः पिनाकधृक्॥ 4.97.10 ॥
4.97.m: and furnished with various kinds of edible foods, he should present to a brāhmaṇa, [saying:] / "May the God of gods, Sadyojāta, wielder of the Pināka, be pleased here."

4.97.s:
pṛṣadājyaṃ ca saṃprāśya svapyādbhūmāvudaṅmukhaḥ ..
pañcadaśyāṃ tataḥ prātaḥ sarvametatsamācaret .. 11 ..
4.97.d:
पृषदाज्यं च संप्राश्य स्वप्याद्भूमावुदङ्मुखः ॥
पञ्चदश्यां ततः प्रातः सर्वमेतत्समाचरेत् ॥ 11 ॥
4.97.m: Having consumed ghee mixed with curd, he should sleep on the ground facing north. / Then, in the morning on the fifteenth day, he should perform all of this:

4.97.s:
tarpayitvā tatonnena brāhmaṇāñchaktitaḥ śubhān ..
suhṛtpadātisahitaḥ paścādbhuñjīta vāgyataḥ .. 12 ..
4.97.d:
तर्पयित्वा ततोन्नेन ब्राह्मणाञ्छक्तितः शुभान् ॥
सुहृत्पदातिसहितः पश्चाद्भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥ 12 ॥
4.97.m: Having then gratified auspicious brāhmaṇas with food according to his means, / he should eat afterwards together with his friends and foot-soldiers, with speech restrained.

4.97.s:
tataḥ kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāmetatsarvaṃ samācaret ..
caturdaśīṣu sarvāsu kuryātpūrvavadarcanam .. 13 ..
4.97.d:
ततः कृष्णचतुर्दश्यामेतत्सर्वं समाचरेत् ॥
चतुर्दशीषु सर्वासु कुर्यात्पूर्ववदर्चनम् ॥ 13 ॥
4.97.m: Then, he should perform all this on the dark fourteenth day. / On all fourteenth days he should perform the worship as before.

4.97.s:
ye ca māse viśeṣāḥ syustānnibodha kramādiha ..
mārgaśīrṣādimāseṣu svapannetānudīrayet .. 14 ..
4.97.d:
ये च मासे विशेषाः स्युस्तान्निबोध क्रमादिह ॥
मार्गशीर्षादिमासेषु स्वपन्नेतानुदीरयेत् ॥ 14 ॥
4.97.m: And learn here in due order whatever particulars exist for each month. / In the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa, lying down he should recite these:

4.97.s:
śaṃkarāya namastubhyaṃ namaste karavīraka ..
tryaṃbakāya namastubhyaṃ maheśvaramataḥ param .. 15 ..
4.97.d:
शंकराय नमस्तुभ्यं नमस्ते करवीरक ॥
त्र्यंबकाय नमस्तुभ्यं महेश्वरमतः परम् ॥ 15 ॥
4.97.m: "Homage to you, O Śaṅkara! Homage to you, O Karavīraka! / Homage to you, O Tryambaka!" Thereafter, "O Maheśvara!"

4.97.s:
namaste'stu mahādeva sthāṇave ca tataḥ param ..
namaḥ paśupate nātha namaste śaṃbhave namaḥ .. 16 ..
4.97.d:
नमस्तेऽस्तु महादेव स्थाणवे च ततः परम् ॥
नमः पशुपते नाथ नमस्ते शंभवे नमः ॥ 16 ॥
4.97.m: "Homage be to you, O Mahādeva!" And thereafter, "to Sthāṇu!" / "Homage, O Paśupati, Lord! Homage to you, O Śambhu, homage!"

4.97.s:
namaste paramānaṃda namaḥ somārddhadhāriṇe ..
namo bhīmāya cogrāya tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ .. 17 ..
4.97.d:
नमस्ते परमानंद नमः सोमार्द्धधारिणे ॥
नमो भीमाय चोग्राय त्वामहं शरणं गतः ॥ 17 ॥
4.97.m: "Homage to you, O Supreme Bliss! Homage to the bearer of the half-moon! / Homage to the Terrific and Fierce One! I have approached you for refuge."

4.97.s:
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhisarpiḥ kuśodakam ..
paṃcagavyaṃ tathā bilvaṃ yavāgūkṣīravārijam .. 18 ..
4.97.d:
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधिसर्पिः कुशोदकम् ॥
पंचगव्यं तथा बिल्वं यवागूक्षीरवारिजम् ॥ 18 ॥
4.97.m: Cow's urine, cow dung, milk, curd, ghee, kuśa water, / the five products of the cow, as well as bilva, barley-gruel, lotus rooted in water,

4.97.s:
tilāṃśca kṛṣṇānvidhivatprāśnīyātsamudāhṛtān ..
pratimāsaṃ caturdaśyāmekaikaṃ prāśanaṃ smṛtam .. 19 ..
4.97.d:
तिलांश्च कृष्णान्विधिवत्प्राश्नीयात्समुदाहृतान् ॥
प्रतिमासं चतुर्दश्यामेकैकं प्राशनं स्मृतम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.97.m: and black sesame seeds prescribed by rule, he should consume as stated. / One by one, their consumption is traditionally ordained on the fourteenth day in each successive month.

4.97.s:
maṃdārairmālatībhiśca tathā dhattūkairapi ..
siṃduvārairaśokaiśca mallikākubjapāṭalaiḥ .. 4.97.20 ..
4.97.d:
मंदारैर्मालतीभिश्च तथा धत्तूकैरपि ॥
सिंदुवारैरशोकैश्च मल्लिकाकुब्जपाटलैः ॥ 4.97.20 ॥
4.97.m: With mandāra and mālatī flowers, and likewise with dhattūras, / with sinduvāras and aśokas, with mallikā, kubja, and pāṭala blossoms,

4.97.s:
arkapuṣpaiḥ kadaṃbaiśca śatapatraistathotpalaiḥ ..
